Tested on large language models tuned from multi-goal judge feedback, it beats every baseline on instruction following and general chat. Trained checkpoints are released at two model sizes.
arxiv-2602-19141:
Can a flattering chatbot drive users toward delusion? Kartik Chandra, with three co-authors, tests that danger in 2026 with modelling and simulation. Users sometimes grow dangerously confident in outlandish beliefs after long chatbot talks. The usual suspect is sycophancy, the chatbot habit of validating user claims.

A simple Bayesian model formalises sycophancy and delusional spiralling. Even an idealised Bayes-rational user proves vulnerable. Sycophancy plays a causal role, not a merely correlational one. Two candidate mitigations fail to stop the effect. Blocking hallucinated false claims does not suffice. Warning users about possible sycophancy does not suffice either. Developers and policymakers thus face a deeper design problem than fact-checking alone.
arxiv-2602-19341:
Driverless ride services promise central fleet control, but their vehicles can run safely only on a suitably equipped subnetwork of roads. Xinling Li and Gioele Zardini ask where robotaxis should operate. They frame the joint choice of service network and fleet capacity under the name AMoD-NDP, the Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Network Design Problem. An operator picks an operation subnetwork and routes all passengers under infrastructure, fleet, and quality-of-service constraints.

The authors give a path-based mixed-integer formulation and a column-generation algorithm that scales to city-sized networks. A master problem optimizes over a limited set of paths, while pricing becomes an elementary shortest path task with resource limits, solved exactly by a custom label-correcting algorithm. The method certifies its optimality gap and extends to a robust version under box uncertainty in travel times.
arxiv-2602-19441:
Autonomous coding agents now submit pull requests on GitHub, but how that work survives human review is little known. Costain Nachuma and Minhaz Zibran study agent-written pull requests in the public AIDev data set, looking at integration outcomes, resolution speed, and collaboration signals at review time. A logit model with errors clustered by repository anchors the number-crunching.

Reviewer attention correlates most strongly with winning integration, while larger change sizes and coordination-breaking actions like force pushes lower the odds of merging. Iteration counts alone explain little once collaboration signals are counted. Close reading shows success when agents join useful review loops that move toward what reviewers expect, so integration depends on collaboration, not code alone.
arxiv-2602-19841:
Insiders sometimes trade on material non-public information, but telling unlawful trades from innocent ones is notoriously hard. A 2026 arXiv paper by Krishna Neupane and four co-authors combines Shapley values with causal forests to detect unlawful insider trading and explain what drives it.

The framework ranks features by their contribution to classification and assesses their causal significance, bringing counterfactual thinking into a domain where correlation alone misleads. Statistically significant links emerge for return, market beta, director status, and price-to-book ratio, pointing to valuation risk, stock performance, market volatility, and information asymmetry. The authors stress that deeper study is still needed to grasp nuanced effects, and that tree models with heterogeneity built in can surface latent structure in trade, finance, and governance data.
arxiv-2602-19941:
The disc around the young star MWC 480 holds rings of dust that may betray forming planets, and new long-wavelength observations sharpen the dust picture. A 2026 arXiv paper led by Yangfan Shi with a large team presents deep, high-resolution Very Large Array observations of the disc, combined with archival ALMA data across several millimetre bands.

The prominent dust ring known as B95 appears at the longest wavelength for the first time, while a faint outer ring stays hidden. Modelling reveals two new annular features, a plateau in the inner disc and a shoulder outside the B95 ring, both consistent with planet-disc interaction. The B95 ring keeps a constant width across wavelengths, and spectral modelling yields two dust families that both fit: compact grains or highly porous grains. The ring holds enough dust mass to assemble giant planet cores.
arxiv-2602-20141:
Mean field games model interactions in large populations. Algorithmic progress has lagged. Model-free methods suffer high variance. Exact methods scale poorly. Hybrid structural methods cut variance while staying tractable, but until now they had not covered partial observability. A 2026 arXiv paper by Clarisse Wibault and eleven co-authors extends them to that setting.

Hybrid structural methods exploit low-dimensional individual state and action spaces plus known transition dynamics. From those, they compute the exact expected return given Monte Carlo rollouts of common noise. The paper proposes Recurrent Structural Policy Gradient, the first history-aware hybrid structural method for mean field games with partial information. It converges an order of magnitude faster than model-free reinforcement learning methods, and it learns history-aware behaviour where hybrid structural methods do not. The authors introduce MFAX, a JAX-based framework for mean field games supporting analytic and sample mean-field updates.
arxiv-2602-20241:
Galaxies grow by trading gas with the halos around them, and metals made in stars ride along. To trace that trade, a 2026 arXiv paper by a large team led by Wuji Wang compares gas chemistry inside galaxies with gas chemistry in their halos. Its targets are typical star-forming galaxies seen at redshifts four to six, observed with JWST and ALMA together.

The sample holds galaxies heavier than about three billion suns. JWST spectra give line ratios for inner gas, within about three kiloparsecs, and for halo gas five to ten kiloparsecs out. Those ratios are the standard tools for judging metal content. Inner and halo gas turn out to hold similar amounts of metals, so halo gas in these early galaxies is already enriched to the level of the gas inside them. A few line ratios differ slightly between the two reservoirs, a nuance the team's statistical tests catch.
arxiv-2602-20341:
Ignacio Amores-Sesar and four co-authors study a security weakness in modular blockchains that split ordering from execution. BFT consensus backs many fast, low-latency blockchains, but execution and validation in consensus slow the chain. Decoupled designs order only metadata while transactions run together, raising speed. The cost: invalid transactions can stay in the ledger, raising storage costs and enabling gaming.

The authors give the first systematic study of this setting and a formal method for the link between consensus and execution. Within it, they name a new attack, gaslighting, and prove a hard trade-off: fending off gaslighting and full resource use cannot both be done for sure in the decoupled model. They discuss a middle model for leader-based protocols that resists gaslighting while keeping speed and low latency. The work maps a speed choice to a concrete security price.
arxiv-2602-20441:
The classical Seifert algorithm builds a Seifert surface for any link in the three-sphere, giving an explicit construction. Geunyoung Kim extends that construction to null-homologous links in arbitrary three-manifolds. The route runs through surgery on framed links in the three-sphere, generalizing an earlier extension by Alegria and Menasco to integral homology three-spheres via Heegaard splittings.

Arbitrary three-manifolds are more general than the three-sphere or homology spheres, so the extension widens the algorithm's reach substantially. Given a link presented by surgery on a framed link in the three-sphere, the method yields its Seifert surface explicitly. The paper thus closes the gap between the classical construction and the general manifold setting.
arxiv-2602-20541:
Fairly splitting whole goods is hard when classic maximin splits may not exist. Hana Salavcova and two co-authors study limited sharing, where each good may go to up to k agents at a cost. Their first result promises exact maximin share splits when goods can be shared with care among at least half the agents, with an even agent count. Odd counts give a weaker promise.

The authors build a Shared Bag-Filling method promising a near maximin share split, with a factor based on sharing cost and limit. It gets exact splits back when the factor hits one. They add Sharing Maximin Share, a fairness idea spreading maximin share to the k-sharing setting. Such splits exist for same values and for two agents, but a counter-case blocks all-case being. A link to limited maximin share gives near promises for it from known results.
arxiv-2602-20741:
M R Turner and D J B Lloyd construct a number scheme for weakly interacting pulses in the two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau equation, needing fast, accurate motion.

The scheme uses a global centre cut, building the solution as pulses plus a rest function square to zero modes of the linear map. Projecting that built form onto the centre surface yields a two-speed system. The system pairs slow plain equations for pulse spots and phases with a fast partial differential rule for the rest function. For separated pulses, the system grows in a small gap value, with the rest function set by a steady partial differential rule solved with GMRES. Results for two to five pulses show different balances, such as stable fixed points and limit cycles. The interaction of two three-pulse structures is considered, where structures tend to split into pairs of pulses moving away from the start.
arxiv-2602-20841:
Knot theory studies surfaces in four dimensions through pictures called motion pictures, and ribbon concordances link one classical knot to another. Eva Horvat and Luka Marcic describe the fundamental quandle of such a surface in this 2026 arXiv paper. They work from the topological definition and derive a presentation of the quandle directly from its motion picture.

Their main result concerns a ribbon concordance from one knot to another. It produces an injective map from the second knot's quandle into the concordance quandle, and a surjective map from the first knot's quandle onto it. These two maps give a clean algebraic shadow of the geometric relation between the knots. Readers get a concrete tool for telling concordances apart.
arxiv-2602-20941:
A quantum measurement yields both a classical outcome and a post-measurement quantum state, and real devices deliver both with flaws. Andres Munoz-Moller, Leevi Leppajarvi, and Teiko Heinosaari ask how much a foe can learn through that flaw in this 2026 arXiv paper. The foe disturbs the device with a hidden measurement, which makes the watcher's tool and the foe's measurement jointly doable.

The authors link the noise in the watcher's device to the facts the foe can pull out, for foes aimed at the same basis or a mutually unbiased basis. In both cases they derive rules that are both needed and enough for fit of a single-qubit flawed tool with a noisy meter. Those rules give the most facts that can be pulled out in terms of the watcher's noise. A device build from the foe's side rounds out the same-basis case.
arxiv-2602-21241:
Nematic liquid crystals are modeled in practice with a tensor model built from a molecule-level model, but that build leaves a spiky entropy term. Baoming Shi, Dawei Wu, Lei Zhang, and Pingwen Zhang map that term in this 2026 arXiv paper. They split it into a spiky but stated leading part and a hidden but regular fix. The fix proves regular enough for true number-based near forms, including by neural nets.

The split yields a handy free energy for working out nematic conduct. Trials show it captures the even-to-ordered shift and free-edge droplet setups. Readers get a build that keeps real trust while dropping a compute and theory snag from the standard tensor model.
arxiv-2602-21341:
Geometry-free view synthesis transformers now lead novel view synthesis, but their scaling behavior with compute is unclear. Evan Kim, Hyunwoo Ryu, Thomas Mitchel, and Vincent Sitzmann map those scaling laws in this 2026 arXiv paper, deriving design principles for compute-optimal models. Contrary to prior findings, encoder-decoder architectures can be compute-optimal; earlier negative results trace to suboptimal choices and unequal compute comparisons.

Across compute levels, their Scalable View Synthesis Model scales as effectively as decoder-only models. It reaches a superior performance-compute frontier and beats the previous state of the art on real-world benchmarks, with substantially reduced training compute. Practitioners get scaling guidance plus an architecture that spends compute where it matters for view synthesis.
arxiv-2602-21441:
Shiwei Tan and five co-authors propose causal decoding to curb false object mentions in image-and-text language models. Such models give detailed vision-language answers but often mention objects absent from the image. That flaw undermines trust in practice. Earlier fixes lean on heuristic penalties, post-hoc correction, or generic decoding tweaks, with limited gains.

Their framework applies targeted causal fixes during generation to weaken spurious links that trigger false object mentions. By reshaping decoding, it cuts false object tokens while keeping descriptive quality intact. Across captioning and question-answering benchmarks, it substantially lowers hallucination rates and reaches state-of-the-art faithfulness without degrading overall output quality.
arxiv-2602-21841:
Federated learning has emerged as a pattern for trustworthy AI through privacy-preserving, spread-out training. Yet it is highly open to hostile attacks harming model integrity and data secrecy, a weakness worsened because standard data checks clash with spread-out design. While blockchain joining has been proposed for some limits, its power against hostile attacks remains untried. Mario García-Márquez and three co-authors introduce Resilient Federated Chain, a blockchain-enabled federated learning setup boosting toughness against such threats.

The setup builds on the Proof of Federated Learning design by reusing redundancy in its Pooled Mining setup as an active defense layer with tough aggregation rules. A flexible scoring function in its consensus setup allows adaptive defense against attack plans. Extensive tests on image sorting under hostile cases show Resilient Federated Chain clearly improves toughness over baselines, offering a workable answer for securing spread-out learning.
arxiv-2602-22041:
When self-driving cars and mobile robots share space with people, blame for a near miss is often spread across many actors at once. Ashwin George and four co-authors note that standard responsibility scores judge agents one by one, and fail when many actors jointly cause an outcome. They propose a metric for the causal responsibility of groups, aimed at filling those gaps.

The paper also defines kinds of assertive influence, agents that push another's path around, and offers a tiering algorithm that picks out which assertive agents matter. Scenario simulations then show how group effects rise and fall with interaction dynamics and with how close agents are. The work gives designers a fairer way to assign responsibility in crowded, shared spaces.
arxiv-2602-22341:
Metric networks, wire-like structures with lengths and positions on every edge, model molecules, light crystals, waveguides, and sound metamaterials. Charles Emmett Maher and two co-authors ask how topological and geometric disorder shapes the spectrum of the differential Laplacian on such networks. They build compact networks from spatial tessellations of hyperuniform point patterns, which suppress large-scale density fluctuations.

Recent software advances make partial differential equations on large, compact networks feasible to analyze, and the team uses them to probe how disorder type shifts spectral features. For makers of wave-guiding devices, the work maps which kinds of disorder matter, and how strongly.
arxiv-2602-22441:
Latent reasoning performs multi-step reasoning in continuous latent space instead of discrete text, promising thought beyond language tokens. Yingqian Cui and nine co-authors analyze how latent-reasoning methods actually behave under weak and strong supervision, a question prior performance studies left open. They identify two key issues that cut across methods and supervision levels.

First, pervasive shortcut behavior: methods reach high accuracy without truly relying on latent reasoning. Second, the team examines whether latent reasoning supports breadth-first-like exploration in latent space. The analysis gives the field a clearer picture of when latent reasoning is real and when it is a shortcut in disguise.
arxiv-2602-22841:
M. Galletti and twelve co-authors demonstrate beam-driven wakefield acceleration inside a laser-plasma filament. Self-guided femtosecond laser pulses in low-pressure gas carve plasma filaments, a fresh base for wakefield acceleration. Unlike schemes needing built or preformed plasma channels, this route exploits nonlinear light-matter interaction directly.

That trick slashes the energy needed to make plasma. It opens tunable stages that could run thousands of pulses per second over metre-scale lengths, with widths down to tens of millionths of a metre. Filament formation also repeats more reliably than discharge plasmas, whose breakdown starts randomly. The team's proof-of-principle run accelerated electron bunches past 250 million volts per metre, matching simulations closely and pointing toward compact, high-rate accelerator facilities.
arxiv-2602-22941:
Julian Ziegler and seven co-authors reconstruct canoe-sprint pacing from broadcast-style video. Velocity and stroke-rate profiles drive peak performance, and GPS, the gold standard, is often unavailable. The framework covers all sprint disciplines and distances from 200 to 500 metres using panned and zoomed recordings.

YOLOv8 detects buoys and athletes, with the known buoy grid yielding homographies for position estimation. A U-net-based boat-tip calibration learns a boat-specific athlete offset, while optical-flow tracking adapts to multi-athlete boats. Stroke rate comes from pose estimates or athlete bounding boxes. Against elite-competition GPS data, velocity error runs about one percent and stroke-rate error under one percent, with very high rank correlation, giving coaches accurate automated feedback without sensors.
arxiv-2602-23141:
Tao Liu and three co-authors stabilize online video without labels or look-ahead, using classical priors. Unlike deep-learning methods needing paired stable and unstable datasets, their approach instantiates the classical stabilization pipeline in three stages with a multithreaded buffering mechanism. That setup is aimed at three lasting problems for learning-based tools: scarce training material, weak user control, and slow running on modest devices.

Current test sets dwell mostly on daytime, forward-facing phone footage in ordinary light, so they leave night-time drone sensing from above without coverage. As a remedy for that missing coverage, the group releases a fresh aerial video collection from drones that mixes several kinds of sensor data, called UAV-Test. In their trials, the approach beats the best live stabilizers on measured scores and on how the footage looks, and it does about as well as tools that work after recording ends.
arxiv-2602-23641:
Weiqi Chen and two co-authors uncover a magnetic duality in the Sun's full-disk field, likened to Janus, the two-faced god. The solar cycle, marked by sunspot activity patterns, anchors heliospheric physics. The research identifies two functionally separate populations: the Strong-Field Group and the Weak-Field Group.

The groups operate in opposing phases regardless of latitude. The Strong-Field-dominated cycle is visually prominent at the solar surface, synchronizing with the sunspot cycle at low latitudes but running in anti-phase at high latitudes. The Weak-Field-driven cycle, its hidden counterpart, opposes the Strong-Field group at both high and low latitudes, a behavior not identified until now. Influenced by these groups, the dual nature permeates the entire solar atmosphere, so full-disk solar activity is globally modulated by the Janus cycle.
arxiv-2602-23941:
Ludovic Moncla and three co-authors introduce EDDA-Coordinata, an annotated dataset of historical geographic coordinates drawn from Diderot and d'Alembert's eighteenth-century Encyclopédie. The 2026 paper addresses a messy recovery task. Old texts express coordinates in varied forms and with uneven precision. That variety complicates automatic extraction from digitized early modern books.

Those gold annotations train transformer models that first spot coordinate-bearing entries, then retrieve and normalize the coordinates. Cross-validation scores are strong, and tests on an out-of-domain French dictionary and a nineteenth-century English encyclopedia show useful transfer, supporting reuse of the pipeline on other historical texts. The set gives the team real cases to learn from. The team then checks the trained models on new texts. Good scores on new texts show the set can travel to other old books.
arxiv-2602-24241:
Saber Zerhoudi and Michael Granitzer present UXSim, a hybrid framework for simulating user search behavior in complex interactive systems. The 2026 paper notes that traditional methods rely on static user proxies. Standalone language-model agents may lack deep, verifiable grounding, and neither captures the dynamism and personalization of real human-computer interaction.

UXSim integrates both approaches: an adaptive language-model agent whose reasoning is informed and constrained by grounded data from traditional simulators. That synthesis enables simulations of user behavior more accurate and dynamic than either approach alone. The framework offers search system designers a way to test interfaces against simulated users.
arxiv-2603-00241: Ortame and colleagues simulate a dwarf galaxy with FABLE physics at high resolution, testing novel sink-based black hole accretion models with relaxed supernova feedback. Sink-based runs accrete more efficiently than traditional Bondi-based runs, and active galactic nucleus feedback drives early, rapid quenching kept up by fast, hot, metal-enriched outflows. That polluted outer gas flattens metallicity gradients all the way to redshift zero. The team also tests two virial estimators, finding wide gaps from true dynamical mass, especially during high-redshift dwarf assembly.
arxiv-2603-00341: Giri describes the Askaryan Radio Array, a South Pole experiment hunting radio flashes from neutrinos striking Antarctic ice. The array has five stations with deep in-ice antennas sensing both vertical and horizontal polarization. With nearly 30 station-years banked, the array now runs its first search for diffuse ultra-high-energy neutrinos. The analysis should yield the tightest in-ice radio limits yet up to one ZeV, and can probe fluxes suggested by KM3NeT near 220 PeV. The results mark a key step toward methods for next-generation detectors.
arxiv-2603-00941: Bhogale and six colleagues rethink speech-recognition scoring for Indian languages, where spelling variants and code-mixing make strict word error rate look harsher than human listeners judge. Their framework builds benchmarks capturing permissible orthographic variants, producing OIWER, a fairer score. Tests show it cuts pessimistic error by 6.3 points on average and closes inflated model gaps, aligning closer to human perception than prior methods.
arxiv-2603-01041: Wang and sixteen co-authors measure element amounts for 7,302 red giant stars in Omega Centauri from MUSE spectra with the DD-Payne neural network. For the first time they map element variation across the whole chromosome diagram used to split star groups, stretching trends to higher metal levels. Chemically enhanced groups carry more barium, nitrogen tracks star age closely, and no known birth story explains every seen link.
arxiv-2603-01341: Boudourides introduces structural hallucination: patterned distortion of idea organization, link shape, and source roots in language model outputs, hidden from sentence-level accuracy checks. To detect it he builds a network-based stress test using knowledge graph extraction, graph match analysis, hub score weighing, and citation soundness checks. Applied to Roget's Thesaurus from 1911, a Wikidata philosophers knowledge graph, and Dimensions.ai citation records, the test finds large drift across all domains, with macro-averaged F1 scores below 0.05 in the word benchmark.
arxiv-2603-01641:
Po-Nien Kung, Zhen Yang, Jeffrey Luo, and colleagues teach language models to use varied reasoning moves on hard problems. Their 2026 work starts from a habit: models repeat small verbal tics, like a pause word that signals a check. Rich chains of such moves are rare in free sampling, so standard training often misses them.

Their frame, Ctrl-R, steers trial runs toward set reasoning patterns during reinforcement learning. Guided runs let the team score how much each trial should count, with no bias in the update. A scaling knob lets the model learn more from bold, off-path trials while training stays stable. Tests show models pick up moves they could not reach before. Gains hold across text-only and vision-language models on math tasks.
arxiv-2603-01841:
Matthieu Latapy and Stephany Rajeh show that simple tools catch injected fake links in interaction streams extremely well. Their 2026 work studies link streams, timed records of contacts in finance, security, and social media. With no ground truth for real anomalies, the field tests detectors on randomly injected links.

Against complex rivals, the pair use trivial graph features plus classical learning methods only. Their basic approach costs very little compute and yields results that stay easy to interpret. Wide experiments probe many other desirable traits of the simple detector, beyond raw scores. The authors conclude the field should now aim at harder anomaly types, not random fakes. Code and data are public, so the claim can be checked and the bar for new methods rises.
arxiv-2603-02041:
Aleksei Dorkin, Taido Purason, Emil Kalbaliyev, and colleagues lift Estonian skill in a model that knows many tongues. Their 2026 work asks if more training on one small tongue can help it without harm to English or to broad reasoning skill. Most large models train on English-heavy text, so small tongues get weak service from the same tools.

They start from an open base model and train it more on a mix with far more Estonian in it. English replay plus code, math, and chat-style data keep the blend close to the first training mix. Fine-tuning and a merge step then add strong skill at taking orders in chat. A broad set of Estonian tests shows gains in tongue skill, facts, reasoning, and translation. English scores stay strong, which backs one-tongue boosts as a sound, workable plan.
arxiv-2603-02241:
Jingqi Lu, Keqi Han, Yun Wang, and Carl Yang benchmark neuron sorting in a tiny worm in this 2026 study. The worm, known as C elegans, has a fully mapped nerve network. The task is to label each neuron as sensory, connector, or motor. Inputs cover cell place, wiring links, and activity over time.

Four graph methods, which learn from the wiring itself, faced four standard methods. Attention-based graph models won clearly on place and wiring inputs. Activity inputs gave weak results for every method tried. The authors blame the low time detail in the activity data. Overall, place and wiring proved the key clues for neuron class. The benchmark backs graph methods for this kind of brain data.
arxiv-2603-02341:
Samuel Khiangte, Triparna Sanyal, Sumantra Sarkar, and Nairita Pal learn simple equations for a turbulent two-fluid mix in this 2026 paper. A droplet of one fluid moves through a second fluid under turbulent forcing. The wobbling boundary between fluids encodes physics across many scales. Full simulations capture that motion but cost a lot of time and computing.

The team compares four interpretable data-driven models on simulation data. Each model first compresses the data, then learns compact equations for boundary motion and droplet acceleration. One method, stochastic Langevin regression, proved most accurate across surface tensions and droplet sizes. It also needed fewer terms than its closest rival, making it cheapest to run. Learned models can even encode traits like surface tension and droplet size.
arxiv-2603-02441:
Mohamed AbdulHameed and Benjamin Beeler simulate heat storage in a nuclear fuel material in this 2026 paper. Uranium mononitride is a candidate fuel whose heat capacity at extreme heat is disputed. Data and models disagree above roughly seventeen hundred kelvin. Heat capacity there bends upward faster than simple theory expects.

The authors ask whether nitrogen defects inside the crystal explain that bend. Large dynamics runs with two different force models track nitrogen motion and defect pairs. Both models show nitrogen growing more mobile as heat climbs. One model yields far more defect pairs, adding a sizable heat term. That defect term matches the bend seen in older data fits. Disorder in the nitrogen sublattice thus likely drives the high-heat behavior.
arxiv-2603-02641:
Szu-Wei Fu, Rong Chao, Xuesong Yang, and colleagues rethink universal speech enhancement in this 2026 paper. Enhancement must restore speech under many kinds of damage while keeping it faithful. Three overlooked choices shape results: training targets, the distortion-perception balance, and data quality. The team addresses each in turn with systematic experiments.

Using early room reflections as the cleaning target hurts perceptual quality and speech recognition, they show. Time-shifted echo-free clean speech makes a superior target instead. A two-stage framework then achieves minimal distortion at a chosen quality level. Large uncurated corpora impose a performance ceiling, since models fail to remove subtle artifacts. Their method leads a major 2025 challenge test set. It also generalizes across languages, aiding text-to-speech data cleaning.
arxiv-2603-02741:
Shinichiro Akiyama reviews recent progress in tensor network methods for physics in this 2026 paper. Tensor networks break huge quantum problems into linked small pieces that a computer can shrink step by step. The review focuses on renormalization group methods, which zoom out while keeping the physics that matters.

These methods avoid the sign and complex-action problems that block other simulation styles. That makes them attractive for lattice field theory, above all for quantum chromodynamics at high heat and density. Akiyama also highlights newer ideas that use conformal field theory insight to probe universal behavior near phase changes. Several topics flagged here are expected to shape coming tensor network studies of strong-force physics.
arxiv-2603-02941:
Jinoh Kim and Jaewon Son shrink the index behind searches like show me cafés open now. Their 2026 algorithm, Timehash, filters businesses by opening hours in large location services. Simple range checks are slow, while indexing every minute explodes the index size.

Timehash builds a layered time index with resolutions that can be tuned to the data, learning the best layering from millions of real business records. A five-level version cut index terms by over ninety-nine percent versus minute-level indexing, with no false hits or misses at all. Tests scaled from one hundred thousand to over twelve million places at flat cost per record. Tricky cases like breaks and irregular hours are handled, and the idea extends to shops and booking systems.
arxiv-2603-03141:
Minjian Zhang and Mahesh Viswanathan predict data races in concurrent programs before they fully unfold. A race happens when two threads access shared data without proper ordering, and short races, where the two accesses sit close together in an execution trace, are the most plausible to recur. Their 2026 paper builds a monitoring framework for spotting them inside a chosen window size.

Algorithms for two race definitions follow. The happens-before version matches a leading tool's speed while using memory tied to the window, not the whole trace. The sync-preserving version runs faster and leaner than its rival. Experiments confirm the trade: less memory, quicker runs, and significantly more races found under the same budget.
arxiv-2603-03241:
Zimo Wen, Boxiu Li, Wanbo Zhang, and colleagues benchmark whether generating an image first helps a model understand it. Unified multimodal models both see and draw, yet nobody had mapped where that generation actually aids understanding. Their 2026 benchmark, UniG2U-Bench, sorts the question into seven regimes and thirty subtasks needing different depths of visual transformation.

Across more than thirty models, unified systems generally scored below their vision-language bases, and answering after generating usually hurt versus answering directly. Consistent gains did appear in spatial intelligence, visual illusions, and multi-round reasoning, where intermediate images genuinely help. Tasks with similar structure, and models with similar architectures, behaved alike. The authors call for richer training data and new paradigms to unlock the unified promise.
arxiv-2603-03441:
Julien Larena turns the clutter around strong gravitational lenses into a cosmological signal. Upcoming stage-four sky surveys will photograph billions of galaxies and, as a bonus, find over a hundred thousand strong lenses. Each lens's light is slightly sheared by matter along the line of sight. His 2026 article proposes measuring that line-of-sight shear as a probe in its own right.

Three new correlation functions follow: the shear with itself, with galaxy positions, and with galaxy shapes. Adding them promotes the standard analysis scheme from three-by-two to six-by-two correlation sets. Larena designs estimators for the new functions, derives their expected values from the matter power spectrum, and works out the full covariance. Across sample scenarios, the signal should be detectable at very high significance, even in the most pessimistic case.
arxiv-2603-03641:
Zhiheng Shi and four colleagues simulate how green routing advice ages as cities grow. Eco-routing cuts one driver's emissions, but whether millions of eco-routes add up, and for how long, was unexplored. Their 2026 study builds two equilibrium models, one where travelers weigh only time, one where they weigh time and carbon. It couples them to demand forecasts and runs six American cities under several population futures.

Eco-routing does cut total emissions. Yet in most cities emissions grow faster than population itself, a superlinear scaling no routing or construction strategy changes. Eco-routed travelers also drift toward shorter routes over time, creating carbon bottlenecks on a few links. Expanding capacity on a tiny targeted set of those links cut emissions modestly and travel time by more than a quarter, without dulling eco-routing's edge.
arxiv-2603-03941:
A study led by Ameya Markale and others uses deep learning to flag image artifacts in high b-value breast diffusion-weighted MRI. Diffusion imaging supports lesion detection and characterization, but high b-value acquisitions often suffer intensity artifacts that can distort diagnosis. The team set out to detect both overly bright and overly dark artifacts, slice by slice, using either binary classification for artifact presence or multiclass classification for artifact intensity.

The retrospective, single-center data set held close to twelve thousand slices from routine 3-tesla breast examinations. Three convolutional networks were trained, and the best, DenseNet121, reached strong discrimination for both artifact types and solid multiclass results on a holdout set. A radiologist scored the predicted bounding boxes, derived from heatmaps, as moderately accurate. The authors conclude the detection is promising but needs further checking before clinical use.
arxiv-2603-04041: Kirsanova and others describe OPTIMus, a survey of massive star-forming regions at optical, infrared, and millimeter bands. Using multi-band data, the team will rebuild three-dimensional structure and real settings of HII zones, photodissociation zones, and nearby molecular clouds. The paper details notes from telescopes of the Special Astrophysical Observatory, the Caucasian Mountain Observatory, and the Onsala Space Observatory.
arxiv-2603-04841: Gurrola, Scherrer, and Trivedi propose probing dark energy with a lunar laser scope. Working field theory of cosmic speedup describes dark energy and modified gravity model-alone, yet many terms stay weakly constrained. Horizon-scale metric wobble reads can probe the kinetic sector straight. Reach extends to the kinetic number and dark energy's linked sound speed. This gives a new viewing handle on tiny fit rules for late-time acceleration models. Broad regions of setting space can thus be probed, constrained, or maybe found.
arxiv-2603-05041: Thomas Pinetz and team offer IRTTA, exploiting middle reconstructions in optical coherence tomography for test-time change of image splitting. Low-cost screening devices use iterative rebuild to rough high-quality counterparts, but downstream scores is judged only on the final image. IRTTA tunes a frozen downstream network's normalization settings through a modulator network conditioned on rebuild timescale, learned at test time with an averaged entropy loss. Change among timestep-wise segmentations yields uncertainty figures at no extra cost, raising splitting without modifying rebuild or the downstream model.
arxiv-2603-05241: Tamara Ranković and colleagues design and implement a monitoring system collecting and aggregating metrics from distributed clouds, where users dynamically create and dispose of tailored ad-hoc clouds. Observability is essential for the model in practice, so node agents collect machine-level, container-level, and application-level metrics. In health checks, that data moves to the cloud's control plane, where it is persisted and served through several APIs, including a streaming one. Node metrics are also aggregated per cloud, giving clients a more comprehensive view of system state.
arxiv-2603-05541: Bello and team present PPCMI-SF for privacy-preserving joint medical image segmentation across sites with mixed sets. Hospitals cannot share scans or labels, and latent-space work still faces limits on how right results are and weakness to attack. Skip-linked autoencoders for images and masks join a latent transform with per-client orthogonal mixing and permutation before sharing. A server mapping network performs multi-scale latent-to-latent mapping for run-time use without raw data. It earns Dice scores and strong defence against inversion and membership attacks.
arxiv-2603-05641: Batra and team present RFM-HRI, a multi-mode data set of robot failures in medical human-robot dealings during crash-cart item fetching tasks. Wizard-of-Oz studies with 41 people logged replies to failure types spanning speech, timing, grasp, and search. The data set holds 214 samples with facial action units, head pose, speech transcripts, plus self-reports. Failures lower feeling valence and felt control, linked to being lost, anger, and upset, while success brings surprise, relief, and trust. Across repeat failures, feelings shift: being lost falls while upset rises.
arxiv-2603-05841: Worley extends Birkhoff's representation theorem from finite distributive lattices to locally finite ones. Birkhoff's theorem matches a finite distributive lattice to the order-ideal lattice of its join-irreducible poset. The main result gives an analogous duality for locally finite distributive lattices. Such a lattice is dual to a pair: a poset of prime filters plus a subset of its order ideals. That subset forms a sublattice of order ideals with finite mutual symmetric differences, containing ideals that both include and exclude each element.
arxiv-2603-05941: Joshi presents a clear AI approach turning raw agent traces into structured, human-clear notes. Coding agents promise auto work, yet fail in ways hard to debug, and general models give only ad-hoc notes. The method combines a failure list, a tagging system with a defined schema, and a hybrid maker making flows, notes, tips. A 20-person study shows root causes found 2.8 times faster and correct fixes proposed with 73 percent higher score than raw traces. The structured approach beats ad-hoc notes through steady insights with built-in views.
arxiv-2603-06241: Johnson and his team study inequalities for function pairs on product domains across two measure spaces. The work treats pairs of functions, not single functions alone. Their main result is a Jensen type inequality in a broad product measure setting, with Hölder and Minkowski inequalities as special cases. The inequality admits sharp equality characterizations plus quantitative, variational, and probabilistic refinements under added convexity assumptions. Corollaries cover power mean, entropy type, and erasure robust cases, plus uses for convolution operators and weighted discrete models.
arxiv-2603-06441: Duan simulates giant radio source formation in dark matter halos under normal gas conditions, despite elusive formation. Hosts sit in halos of 10 to the 13th, 14th, and 15th solar masses, with hot gas fractions and varied profiles. Successful formation under normal gas fractions shows an unusually low-density environment is not required. Lobe propagation slows at extreme central density and pressure: weak pressure collimates jets poorly, strong pressure strengthens jet-medium interaction. Most sources in the two lower halo masses reach radio powers comparable to observations at similar scales.
arxiv-2603-06741: Jiang and colleagues present a cheaper, mixed-objective way to train decentralized diffusion models. Earlier decentralized training demanded huge compute and one shared objective across experts. Their frame lets experts use different objectives, DDPM or Flow Matching, unified at inference with no retraining, converts pretrained checkpoints across objectives, and uses a lean AdaLN-Single design. On LAION-Aesthetics it cuts compute and data sharply while beating the uniform baseline on quality and diversity.
arxiv-2603-06941: Imbens and colleagues study adaptive experiments aimed at showing effects, not precise estimation. Platforms, health care, and social science often need only to show one candidate intervention helps some group on some outcome. They frame that goal as testing a global null in a threshold bandit setting. Two inference procedures stay valid under general adaptive sampling: pooling data across promising arms, and time-uniform multiple testing of arm means. A moderate-deviations rule for the sequential t-statistic backs confidence sequences when arm counts are large against sample size.
arxiv-2603-07541: Lu and Peng take up representations of shifted super Yangians, and of finite W-superalgebras of type A. They give a test for when irreducible modules are finite-dimensional in the standard parity case. A Gelfand-Tsetlin character formula for Verma modules, spelled out, follows for the finite W-superalgebras. Centers for even nilpotent elements of one general linear Lie superalgebra all match the center of the universal enveloping superalgebra.
arxiv-2603-07641: Takalo builds oscillatory reconstructions from zeros of Dirichlet L-functions to show how primes split by congruence class. They act as analytic filters, with zero rates making clear peaks at prime powers. For modulus five, conjugate character pairs cancel in patterns mirroring algebraic relations between characters. Joining all of them modulo five, only primes congruent to one modulo five survive, showing the cyclotomic split as an interference pattern.
arxiv-2603-07841: Pham and colleagues tackle a hard test problem for systems that turn plain questions into database queries. When a new set of data has no checked answers, teams cannot tell if a fresh model is sound. Their tool, FusionSQL, works with any such system and gauges its hit rate from the shape of its own outputs, showing how the new data drifts from the training data. Tests across varied tasks show its gauge tracks true hit rates and flags slips early.
arxiv-2603-07941: Haeuser and colleagues show the spin-charge structure behind colossal magnetoresistive switching in spin devices. Imaging it demands strong fields, cryogenic cold, and nm resolution, a mix that had kept its fine dynamics unseen. Their cryogenic magneto-terahertz microscope tracks the terahertz change of the switch in a manganite crystal, catching the flip of an antiferromagnetic insulator into a ferromagnetic metal. Imaging plus a model shows the switch starting from spin-flip sites a few nm wide at low fields, merging into regions roughly 15 nm across near the threshold.
arxiv-2603-08241: Loncour and colleagues study how sensitive language model explanations are to training randomness. Transformer models anchor language processing, yet explaining their decisions remains hard. Recent work showed that the same model trained on the same data with different randomness can yield very different explanations. The authors test how syntactic context, the classes to be learned, and the tasks shape this sensitivity. All three matter in a statistically significant way: least for syntactic context, mid for the classes, and most for the tasks.
arxiv-2603-08341: Lubitzsch and colleagues build ERASE, testing unlearning as recommender systems use it. It means stripping data from a model, for privacy, security, and liability, yet current benchmarks lean on collaborative filtering and miss sequential work and efficiency. ERASE spans next-basket, session-based, and filtering tasks, with real-use cases removing private interactions or spam. Seven methods, nine data sets, and nine models yield over 600 GB of files and a thousand checkpoints. Approximate unlearning can match retraining but varies widely. Repeated runs strain methods most for attention and recurrent models.
arxiv-2603-08441: Gomes and colleagues compute black hole shadows in nonminimally coupled Weyl connection gravity, a metric-affine extension of general relativity. Spacetime carries a metric plus a Weyl vector field for non-metricity. With a non-dynamical Weyl vector, the field equations stay second order, and the theory admits Schwarzschild-like and Reissner-Nordström-like solutions shifted by a Weyl integration constant. Matching the shadow radii against Event Horizon Telescope limits on Sgr A* sets bounds on the Weyl parameter, showing horizon-scale images already constrain spacetime non-metricity.
arxiv-2603-08841: András Grabarits and Adolfo del Campo track quantum magic across phase transitions under slow driving. Stabilizer Rényi entropies and Pauli spectrum cumulants scale as power laws in the driving rate. The log Pauli spectrum turns out Gaussian, so Pauli values follow a lognormal law, with exact Ising results and long-range Kitaev approximations backing the picture.
arxiv-2603-08941: Noga Ron-Zewi and Mor Weiss show that zero-knowledge codes and quantum CSS codes coincide. Zero-knowledge codes leak nothing from a few codeword symbols, while CSS codes enable quantum error correction. In this short note they prove the two linear, perfect code families are equivalent, then use the link to build explicit good zero-knowledge locally testable codes.
arxiv-2603-09041: Aqib Gul offers AgroDesign, a Python tool that puts experimental design at the heart of farm statistics. Hand-set models, error-term picks, and subjective interaction calls invite wrong reads and mixed reports. The tool turns designs straight into valid line models, finds error strata, tests claims, splits means, checks model basics, and gives decision-ready reads, cutting analyst-driven model picks.
arxiv-2603-09441: Shin Hattori proves an autoduality result for Drinfeld modules of rank two with a stated level structure. Over schemes and algebras satisfying the paper's conditions, any such module is isomorphic to its Taguchi dual. The level structure is of Gamma-1 type twisted by a subgroup meeting a bijectivity condition. As an application, Hattori gives a dual Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism for the Hodge bundle on the Drinfeld modular curve, contrasting with the usual form where the dual module appears.
arxiv-2603-09641: Arash Shahmansoori introduces PRECEPT, a framework that unifies test-time adaptation for language model agents that store knowledge as natural language. Such agents lose retrieval quality as condition counts grow, compose rules unreliably, and cannot spot stale knowledge. PRECEPT pairs exact-match rule retrieval over structured keys with conflict-aware memory that tracks source reliability and invalidates stale rules. Its COMPASS outer loop evolves prompts under Pareto guidance, judged through the same execution pipeline, and tests show large first-try gains.
arxiv-2603-09741: Francesco Ragusa and a large team release ENIGMA-360, a data set of worker activity filmed in a real industrial setting. Paired head worn and fixed camera videos, time matched in both views, carry time and space labels. The set supports three tasks: splitting actions in time, naming key steps and spotting hand object contact. Current top methods struggle on all three tasks.
arxiv-2603-09941: Isaac A. García and Jaume Giné take a new route to Poincaré's classical centre problem for planar vector fields. The problem asks when a monodromic singularity of an analytic family is truly a centre. They prove that, generically, each analytic centre has a Laurent inverse integrating factor in weighted polar coordinates. From this they derive a practical procedure for the parameter conditions that mark centres, and apply it to stubborn families.
arxiv-2603-10041: Ondřej Lukáš and coauthors test whether autonomous cyber attack agents generalise when a network's addresses change. Agents train on five IP range variants of one enterprise scenario and face a sixth, unseen one. Traditional reinforcement learners and adaptation agents degrade sharply, with only partial transfer from some methods. Prompt driven language model agents score highest on the held out variant, at the cost of more compute and loop prone behaviour.
arxiv-2603-10141: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Lihui Liu and Shengguo Zhu study finite time implosion for the three dimensional degenerate compressible Navier Stokes equations. Whether smooth solutions can blow up is a central open question, and recent work shows the answer hinges on how viscosity depends on density. For power law viscosity below a threshold set by the adiabatic exponent, they construct smooth positive starting data whose solutions implode at the origin. Density grows without bound in finite time.
arxiv-2603-10241: Cantarini, Gambini and Zaccagnini study the discrete convolution of the Liouville function with itself. That convolution counts representations of an integer as a sum of two parts weighted by Liouville values, a Goldbach type counting function. Following a general approach from recent work, they derive a formula, in explicit form, for weighted averages of this count. The formula yields facts about its Dirichlet and power series, and about convolutions with more factors.
arxiv-2603-10541: Caroline Magg and co-authors benchmark promptable foundation models for musculoskeletal CT segmentation, asking how sensitive they are to the human touch in prompts. Eleven models were tested with 2D and 3D prompting on private and public data, covering bone and implant tasks in four regions. The best 2D and 3D models differed, and scores varied widely. Human prompts from an observer study lowered performance versus ideal prompts drawn from labels, and every model reacted to prompt changes. Choosing a model for human-driven use, they conclude, stays hard.
arxiv-2603-10641: Eirik Høyheim and co-authors present a method to detect and remove backdoors in neural networks by tracing active paths through the model. A backdoored model acts normally on clean inputs but obeys an attacker when a trigger appears, and finding such triggers is notoriously hard. Their approach follows the paths a network actually uses, giving an explainable route to spotting the trigger's effect. Tests inject backdoors into a model used for intrusion detection and give promising evidence.
arxiv-2603-10741: C Guillet and co-authors present a solver for simulating lattice structures that are nonlinear and hyperelastic, the materials additive manufacturing now makes practical. Such structures hold thousands of intricate cells, so full simulation is costly. Their method exploits the cells' self-similarity: a few key cells express all local tangent operators as combinations. A FETI-DP preconditioner then keeps the solve fast and nearly matrix-free. Tests cut runtimes from hours to tens of minutes, with large memory savings.
arxiv-2603-10941: Vinícius Litvinoff Justus and Felipe Fontana Vieira revisit the partial copula. This tool was built to test conditional independence. They use it to describe dependence after a covariate's influence is removed. They show it acts as a nonlinear analogue of partial correlation. They prove how features of the underlying conditional copulas limit its shapes. Those shapes are the ones the partial copula can take. Simulations illustrate the results. They point to uses in causal inference. One use is recovering the true sign of a causal effect.
arxiv-2603-11141: Huilin Tai frames cross-species prediction of antimicrobial resistance as an out-of-distribution problem: models trained on some taxa must work on distant genomes that may resist by unlike mechanisms. A strict species-holdout test shows a strong interpretable k-mer model falling apart once species change. That pushes the work toward foundation model embeddings. Tests locate a boundary in the deeper layers where stability breaks. Summing per-window embeddings with MiniRocket preserves local activation patterns. It lifts generalization for local resistance cases.
arxiv-2603-11341: Vernon Barger presents Unified Flavor. It gives quark and lepton masses and mixings a dynamical origin in TeV-scale vectorlike fermion chains. A flavon field enforces ninths-quantized lattice exponents on the couplings. Each Yukawa entry sums over paths along neighbor chains. It factorizes into entry, propagation, and exit amplitudes. Several chains interfere to yield order-one complex coefficients, whose phases source CP violation. The hierarchy emerges from the exponent algebra. Flavor-changing currents stay suppressed. The same symmetry protects the Peccei-Quinn axion's quality.
arxiv-2603-11741: Kala studies the shadow of a Bonanno-Reuter black hole sitting in a plasma medium. This spacetime carries quantum gravity corrections through a scale-dependent parameter, written omega-tilde. Kala computes the shadow's angular radius and tracks how it shifts with omega-tilde and the plasma index. Against the classical Schwarzschild limit, the shadow deviates in systematic ways. Event Horizon Telescope views of Sgr A* then bound omega-tilde. Plasma and quantum-gravity effects blur together in the data, a degeneracy the next-generation EHT may break.
arxiv-2603-12241: Caraci, Knowles, Ranallo, and Torres Giesteira prove that a trapped Bose gas tends to a Euclidean field theory. Their gas is two-dimensional, interacting, and held by a trapping potential in a grand canonical state. As density grows large and interaction range shrinks, the Gibbs state nears the quartic field theory. Relative partition functions converge, and reduced density matrices converge in strong norms. Divergent counterterms here are functions, not scalars, which adds real difficulty over the torus case. Fresh bounds on Green functions for Schrödinger operators support the proof.
arxiv-2603-12641: Huacheng Zeng and co-authors set out a vision for OFDM waveforms in monostatic integrated sensing and communication for 6G. Sensing and communication together are seen as a core 6G technology. Yet monostatic use of OFDM, where one device both sends and senses, remains underexplored. The authors give practical routes to radar-like ranging, Doppler estimates, and scene awareness on communication devices. They close with open research directions meant to speed adoption.
arxiv-2603-12741: Amandine Caut and co-authors propose prompt cards as a standard way to document prompt engineering work. Prompts can be long and complex, and judging them on subjective tasks is hard. A prompt card records goals, design choices, context steps, evaluation practice, and ethical points. The authors show the idea on wordalisation, where structured numbers are turned into text. Cards, they argue, aid reproducibility and transparency. They can also serve as an alternative to benchmarks for judging text quality.
arxiv-2603-13241: Edouard Lansiaux, Idriss Jairi, and Hayfa Zgaya-Biau present a hybrid impurity measure for decision trees. Their Integrated Tsallis Combination joins Tsallis entropy with a polarization term. Entropy gives the information base, while the polarization part reacts to skewed class shares. They prove concavity under stated conditions and set proper boundary values. On seven datasets against 23 rival measures, a plain Tsallis variant had the best accuracy. Their measure stayed close and adds strong theory plus flexible settings.
arxiv-2603-13541: Victor F. Rocha and co-authors propose UDDTECC, a fusion method for ensemble classifier chains. Multi-label methods based on ensembles work well, and Ensemble of Classifier Chains is a widely used one. Its decision template fusion treats each label on its own, with no use of links between labels. The new method fuses with those links in mind, using labels that are conditionally dependent on the one being classified. Tests against two classic fusion schemes and a stacking scheme show gains on most metrics.
arxiv-2603-13641: Quanyan Zhu and Zhengye Han study Berk-Nash equilibria in infinite-horizon MDPs via mathematical programming. Their setting is sequential choice when the model class inside the agent's head is misspecified. Stable behavior is a fixed point: the agent acts optimally for a subjective model that fits the long-run data its own policy creates. They pin down this equilibrium with coupled linear programs and a bilevel optimization formulation. Entropy regularization gives a unique soft Bellman fixed point and a smooth objective. An online learning scheme follows.
arxiv-2603-13741: Jae Yong Lee and co-authors present Ego-1K, a large-scale multiview video dataset for egocentric vision. It holds nearly 1,000 short egocentric videos from a custom rig with 12 synchronized cameras around a 4-camera VR headset. Scene content focuses on hand motions and hand-object interactions in varied settings. The team describes rig design, data processing, and calibration in detail. Experiments show large disparities and image motion from close dynamic objects challenge existing 3D and 4D view synthesis methods. The dataset supports benchmarking of egocentric scene reconstruction.
arxiv-2603-13841: Adhikari, Naia, and Serra prove new results in Euclidean Ramsey theory about colored points in the plane. A classic result by Graham says any finite coloring of the plane holds a one-color triangle of any given area. The authors study rainbow versions, where vertices carry distinct colors. They show that any 3-coloring of the integer lattice yields a rainbow triangle of area one half, or a one-color rectangle of any set area. Related results pair one-color rectangles with rainbow trapezoids of fixed area.
arxiv-2603-14141: Im, Topcu, and Fridovich-Keil study correlated equilibria when agents' costs are known only with uncertainty. A coordinator suggests moves that no agent wants to defy, but wrong cost data can break that promise. Their chance-constrained version keeps the promise with a set confidence level. Sensitivity results price the value of cutting each source of uncertainty. Higher confidence is not always better, since it trades against system efficiency. In tests, the method cuts realized coordination costs by up to 35 percent.
arxiv-2603-14341: Kumar, Sundaram, and Sural present LANTERN, a tool that turns access control audit logs into plain-language policies. Formal ABAC rules are flexible but hard for non-specialists to read. Past tools extract machine rules from logs without bridging to human intent. LANTERN uses large language models to close that gap. The framework checks how far model power carries both accuracy and scale in this translation. A public web app lets others reproduce the results.
arxiv-2603-14841: Roy and co-authors turn binary crash classifiers into live 0-100 driver safety scores with SafeDriver-IQ. Binary risk flags give drivers little to act on. Their frame blends national crash records with Waymo motion scenarios. Domain-informed features and a literature-based calibration layer shape the score. Vulnerable road users enter the risk picture directly. Fifteen checks show the score splits high- and low-risk driving well. Most crashes mix several risk factors, 87% in their count. Combined factors push risk to 4.5 times baseline.
arxiv-2603-15941: Johnny and co-authors chase fair, sturdy CT diagnosis across sites and groups. Chest CT classifiers suffer when scanners or patient mixes shift. Their stack pairs a light MobileViT encoder with a SliceTransformer aggregator. Training uses KL-regularised group robust optimization over sites and subgroups. The KL term stops group weights from collapsing mid-training. Task one sorts COVID-19 cases across many sites. Task two sorts four lung pathologies with gender fairness targets. Scores beat top challenge entries on both tasks, they report.
arxiv-2603-16041: Chen, Guo, and Li size studies that lean on machine-predicted outcomes. Prediction-powered inference gives valid tests from partly labeled data. Classic power formulas ignore the predicted half of the data. Their work asks how many labels a set power truly needs. Closed forms follow from the estimator's large-sample variance. Wald test inversion turns variance into required label counts. Two-sample tests and 2x2 risk tables both get formulas. Label savings scale with prediction R squared, a handy rule. Three biomedical cases show the framework at work.
arxiv-2603-16141: Fan and co-authors train drone swarms that relay under patchy radio links. Real swarms see partial views and drop peer contact often. Their graph-based learning trains central but executes local. Each drone runs a shared policy from nearby messages alone. An SNR threshold graph defines who counts as a neighbor. Attention modules encode local state and fold in messages. The DroneConnect task tests cooperative relay placement. Coverage beats MAPPO by about 12 percent under limits. Scores stay near an offline full-view upper bound.
arxiv-2603-16341: Cai and co-authors detect objects in remote sensing images with PKINet-v2. Targets vary wildly in shape and size, which strains older backbones. Strip kernels suit slender targets but can blur regular shapes. Large square kernels add context yet bring background noise. Their backbone mixes both kernel types in one design. A re-parameterization step fuses the branches for fast inference. Tests on four benchmarks led the field, with 3.9 times faster frames than version one.
arxiv-2603-16541: Cao studies p-biharmonic maps whose domain is a gradient Ricci soliton. The results are Liouville theorems for these maps. Liouville theorems pin down when such maps must be trivial. The setting matters because solitons bend the domain geometry. Special attention goes to one named case. That case is the two-dimensional cigar soliton. It serves as the focus of the deepest results.
arxiv-2603-16641: He, Li, and Chen teach models to name unseen attribute-object pairs. Compositional learning recombines traits and objects seen apart. Prompt tuning on vision-language models builds pairs only implicitly. Features for trait, object, and pair also stay tangled. Their FlowComposer learns two flows toward trait and object text. A learnable Composer fuses the two velocity fields into one. Leaked features are reused as extra training signals. Plugged into baselines, scores rose across three benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-16741: Kothe and co-authors infer mental-health traits from brain and behavior in association tests. The standard D-score uses reaction times alone and predicts weakly. Their sparse hierarchical Bayesian model fuses neural and behavioral signals. Two test variants cover suicidality and psychosis experiences. The model reached AUCs of 0.73 and 0.76 in the best setups. D-scores, by contrast, sat near chance in both tasks. Restricting one test to depression cases improved results further. Larger cohorts must confirm clinical value, they caution.
arxiv-2603-17341: Baba presents a new way to map gas in the inner Milky Way. The method uses motion in a barred galaxy model instead of plain circular rotation. It builds face-on maps of molecular gas from survey data and tests them on simulations first. The maps remove long streak artifacts and show a bar-shaped, uneven inner galaxy, he reports. Gas density falls off past about four kiloparsecs, with a gap closer in and a dense center.
arxiv-2603-17541: Zhang and co-authors study what video fine-tuning does to multimodal language models. Across designs, scales, and frame counts, one pattern repeats. Video scores rise, while static image scores stall or slip, they find. More sampled frames help video but not images. Their instruction-aware Hybrid-Frame method shifts frame counts by task and softens the trade-off. Keeping spatial skill during video training stays the open problem.
arxiv-2603-17641: Parthasarathy and co-authors let evolution design algebraic multigrid cycles. Multigrid solves many PDEs at top speed, but only with well-chosen parts. Their search breeds cycles from proven building blocks with genetic programming. A grammar shapes the space, which allows level-wise smoothing and odd cycling patterns. Hand search could never cover that space. Tests with the hypre library show gains as solver and preconditioner, they report.
arxiv-2603-18041: Bailey asks whether time data can recover geometry lost by a persistence diagram for swarm shapes. For points on a sphere under full consensus flow, two zero-dimensional snapshots suffice. He proves generic local recovery up to rotations and permutations. Edge inner products and their first time rates span the full formation space for every tree type. The work also gives a verified inverse, time bounds, and clear limits from reflection ambiguity.
arxiv-2603-18941: Alves and co-authors sort deep learning methods that spot faults in multi-channel time data. The field has grown fast but lacks a shared map. Their scheme uses eleven traits split across input, output, and model groups. Traits came from method studies and past reviews. They test the scheme on a fresh set of recent papers. Results show a drift toward transformer models and rebuild or forecast methods. The scheme is built to take new traits as the field grows.
arxiv-2603-19041: Lucena and co-authors estimate autoregressive time series models with a neural network in place of classic fits. Classic methods can be slow and fail to settle. Their network bakes the lag structure into a feedforward form, so training by backpropagation yields the coefficients. The lag weights stay readable, which keeps the model clear. In tests on 125,000 fake series, the network recovers coefficients every time. A classic method fails in over half the cases. When both work, accuracy is near equal, but the network is far faster.
arxiv-2603-19441: Dyda and co-authors improve the radiation force math used in simulations of disk winds from active galaxies. Their flux-averaged force multiplier is computed across four light bands, from infrared to X-rays. Ultraviolet light drives most line pushing, as expected. The optical and X-ray bands still add real gains in mass flow and speed. A grey method that averages over bands misses these gains entirely. The results strengthen the case for band-aware radiation physics in wind studies. Photoionization models feed the force values per band.
arxiv-2603-19841: Dash, Bode, and Aditya build a graph neural network for large-eddy simulation of turbulent flames. Such simulations need models for filtered chemical production rates that the resolved fields miss. Their network reads filtered mass fractions and temperature on uneven meshes. Training data come from direct simulations of hydrogen-methane jet flames. The model trains on two fuel blends and is tested on an unseen third blend. It beats an unclosed baseline and a convolutional network. It also holds up at new filter widths without retraining.
arxiv-2603-20041: Cital and Holubec show that a tiny heat engine can strongly break the thermodynamic uncertainty relation. That relation trades current precision against entropy production in steady states. Their engine pairs a discrete ratchet with an underdamped harmonic oscillator as internal control. With a clear split of time scales, the model becomes exactly solvable. The uncertainty ratio then depends on the oscillator's zero-crossing statistics. Sharper internal control pushes the ratio near zero. The engine still runs near maximal current and efficiency in that regime.
arxiv-2603-20341: Rachidi and co-authors aim to keep myeloma survival models both accurate and readable. Opaque models slow uptake in health care, despite strong predictive promise. They train models on Helsinki hospital data for 812 patients. Two penalty schemes keep predictions close to trusted, simpler guides. One guide is a two-feature logistic model; the other is the standard staging system. Test accuracy reached 0.721, and SHAP checks showed sound feature use. The approach makes model behavior easier for clinicians to trust.
arxiv-2603-20641: Liu and Xiu study how observables of a dynamical system change over time. For linear systems, observables obey a closed equation of their own. Its least order comes from the system and the observation map. This gives both a closure and a delay form of the dynamics. For nonlinear systems they define diminishing ambiguity. Long output records can then pin down the observable's motion well. The work shows when past outputs alone can reveal system behavior.
arxiv-2603-20841: Wu develops a Karhunen-Loève framework for channel analysis in fluid antenna systems. These antennas switch among many packed ports for spatial diversity. The channels across ports are strongly correlated, which blocks exact outage math. His method splits the channel into independent eigenmodes. Keeping just the top modes shrinks the outage problem a lot. Closed forms cover the rank one and rank two cases. He proves the truncation always overestimates outage, a safe bias. Only a few modes matter, set by the aperture size, not the port count.
arxiv-2603-21041: Nam studies how a hot hadronic medium changes a rare three-body decay of the K1(1270) meson. The decay goes to two pions and a kaon. He builds the decay amplitude from effective interactions led by rho and K-star pole terms. Heat effects tied to partial chiral symmetry restoration enter through a smooth interpolation. As temperature rises, the parent mass drops and squeezes the decay phase space. The Dalitz pattern deforms, and the decay width falls sharply. He proposes shape measures for later comparison with experiment.
arxiv-2603-21341: Kim and co-authors present RoboAlign, a training framework that aligns language reasoning with low-level robot actions. Vision-language-action models often gain little from VQA style supervision of the base model. RoboAlign samples action tokens through zero-shot natural language reasoning. Reinforcement learning then refines that reasoning to improve action accuracy. After supervised fine tuning, RL alignment on under one percent of the data lifts scores sharply on LIBERO, CALVIN, and real robot tests.
arxiv-2603-21641: Huang and co-authors present mcp-sec-audit, a toolkit for auditing servers built on the Model Context Protocol. That protocol links language models to outside tools and data. Servers often expose risky powers, like file access, network calls, and command runs. The toolkit scans Python-based servers with rule-based pattern matching. It also fuzzes them inside a Docker sandbox while eBPF watches behavior. Each finding comes with a fix suggestion. The goal is to flag over-privileged tool powers before attackers abuse them.
arxiv-2603-21741: The H.E.S.S. Collaboration presents fifteen years of gamma-ray burst follow-ups with its telescopes in Namibia. The array can swing onto a burst within tens of seconds, catching late prompt and early afterglow light above 100 GeV. From 2004 to 2019, no burst gave a firm signal beyond two known detections. The null results form the largest set of very-high-energy upper limits for bursts. Detected bursts tend to be X-ray bright with favorable distance and viewing conditions. Next-generation arrays should catch fainter, farther bursts.
arxiv-2603-21841: Jakl and Reggio examine the axioms behind arboreal categories, a framework built to capture game comonads in logic. Game comonads give a shared view of many model-comparison games. The authors show that one axiom, stating that paths are connected, does not work as intended. They propose a new notion, tree-connectedness, to repair the gap. Under the new definition, all the key properties of arboreal categories that they know of still hold. They also prove that the path functor is a Street fibration.
arxiv-2603-22541: Meilijson studies last passage percolation when the random weights are identically distributed but not independent. On a grid, the passage time is the heaviest upward or rightward path between two points. He asks which joint arrangement of the weights makes expected passage times largest in the convex sense. For mean-one exponential weights he finds an extremal coupling with a clean closed form. He also shows how small the times and their spread can be made. The contrast with the classic independent case is stark.
arxiv-2603-23041: Cardoso and co-authors present HUydra, a system that synthesizes full-range lung CT scans. Computer-aided diagnosis needs more data than clinics can share. Full Hounsfield range scans are hard to model at once. HUydra splits the job by HU interval, training generators on tissue-focused windows. A learned network then merges the parts into one scan. Multi-head designs capture texture while keeping anatomy consistent. The best variant beats standard baselines on image quality scores. It also lowers model size and compute cost.
arxiv-2603-23141: PT, Sardar, and Sardar characterize relatively hyperbolic groups through their boundaries. They work with a finitely generated group and a finite set of subgroups. A cusped space is built from that data. The pair is non-elementary relatively hyperbolic exactly when a boundary condition holds, they prove. Either the Morse boundary or the contracting boundary of the cusped space must be non-empty and compact. The result ties an algebraic trait to boundary shape.
arxiv-2603-23441: Iuliano and three co-authors build MuSe, a mutation testing plugin for the Remix IDE. Remix is the main workbench for writing Ethereum smart contracts. Mutation testing seeds fake faults to grade how strong a test suite is. No such plugin existed for Remix before, despite the high stakes of contract bugs. MuSe packs classic, Solidity-specific, and security-focused mutation operators. It plugs straight into the IDE with no extra setup. Developers can now grade their suites and hunt contract flaws in place.
arxiv-2603-23741: Worley restates a process given by Stanley for building special lattices in mathematics. The process proves that exactly one d-differential distributive lattice exists for each positive whole number d. Worley shows the same idea extends to other finitary distributive lattices with varied structures. It can serve as a tool to construct such lattices or to analyze them. He also uses it to prove facts about weighted-differential lattices with positive weights, hoping it may lead to a full characterization.
arxiv-2603-24041: Tan and co-authors present DeepIn, a neural network that learns the smallest representation it needs. Deep networks predict well but hide their logic, partly because they carry too many parameters. DeepIn finds the minimal representation dimension, picks the relevant variables, and recovers a minimal network shape. Its error rates are provably optimal and adapt to that learned dimension. The framework also supports formal tests on chosen variables and representations. On biomedical and vision benchmarks, it cuts error by up to 30 percent while exposing readable patterns.
arxiv-2603-24241: Daubt and Redder present C-STEP, a safety measure for physics-informed reinforcement learning in mobile robots. Safe navigation in complex settings is still hard for learning agents. Their measure judges safety from the agent's own state, such as its starting velocity, and from forward dynamics. Added to standard navigation rewards, it forms an intrinsic reward that favors both task success and collision avoidance. In numerical tests, collisions fall and robots keep more distance from obstacles. Travel time rises only slightly, they report.
arxiv-2603-24341: Lehr and co-authors measure the low-energy dipole response of the neutron-rich nucleus helium-8. Weak binding and spread-out neutron density give such drip-line nuclei a distinct dipole pattern. The team extracts the total dipole strength below 15 MeV from Coulomb-excitation data. It comes to 0.95 square efemtometers, with a polarizability of 0.61 cubic femtometers. They include the four-neutron decay channel for the first time. Two-neutron emission dominates even above that threshold, pointing to a helium-6 plus two-neutron structure. No four-neutron correlation signal appears.
arxiv-2603-24441: Bollmann and Hess develop a benchmarking scheme for Decoded Quantum Interferometry, a quantum algorithm for certain optimisation problems. Their scheme counts the quantum gates needed to reach an optimal solution. They apply it to the Binary Paint Shop Problem and compare the quantum method against a state-of-the-art classical solver. To do so, they give an explicit circuit construction for a greedy decoder. The decoder handles low-density parity check codes that arise from max-2-XORSAT problems, making the comparison concrete.
arxiv-2603-24541: Bu and co-authors present SEGAR, a framework for generative augmented reality. The idea is to predict future image frames with deliberate visual edits built in, then cache them instead of rendering each frame from scratch. A diffusion-based world model generates the augmented frames, editing chosen regions while preserving others. A correction stage then aligns safety-critical regions with real observations, keeping the intended edits elsewhere.
