Driving scenes serve as the test setting, where region structure is clear and live feedback is easy to obtain.
arxiv-2603-24641: Starepravo and co-authors learn mesh-free discrete operators with a self-supervised graph network. Classical meshless operators trade low cost against rough results, or pay heavily for exact ones. Their framework trains the network with polynomial moment constraints from Taylor expansions. The model maps local stencil positions to operator weights. The learned operators depend only on local geometry, ignore resolution, and transfer across particle setups and equations. Tests show lower error than smoothed particle hydrodynamics and a good balance of cost and error.
arxiv-2603-24741: Kjellgren and co-authors model the diffuse gamma-ray sky of a Milky Way analogue. Gamma rays trace cosmic rays, but the observed sky depends on the gas layout and the observer's position. Using the Rhea suite, they compute pion-decay emission for many observer spots, including inside Local-Bubble-like cavities. The galaxy matches Milky Way luminosities and spectral slopes with no tuning. Total brightness stays stable, yet the sky's morphology shifts strongly with observer location. Angular power spectra track gas column density, not the smoother cosmic ray density.
arxiv-2603-25141: Voigt's notes give an introduction to the theory of quantum symmetries. The theory studies symmetry in a quantum form, beyond the classic groups that act on a space. These notes cover symmetries of sets, both finite and infinite in size. They also treat graphs, where the points and links carry the structure. A third setting is locally compact spaces, a broad class used across analysis. The notes are written as an entry point for readers new to the field.
arxiv-2603-25841: Pham, Nguyen, and Le present GazeQwen, a light way to give a video model access to eye gaze. Current multimodal models use gaze cues poorly, even when they are drawn on the video. GazeQwen adds a small gaze resampler with one to five million trainable parameters. It mixes video features with fixation positions and nudges hidden states inside the language model. On the StreamGaze benchmark, it reaches 63.9 percent accuracy. That beats the same backbone with gaze prompts by 16.1 points, and GPT-4o by 10.5 points.
arxiv-2603-26541: Deng and co-authors present OVI-MAP, a system for open-vocabulary 3D instance mapping as an agent explores. A useful map must segment objects, run in real time, and accept free-form labels. Past methods often assume a closed label set or fuse language data at every pixel, which hurts scale. OVI-MAP splits the job: it builds a class-free 3D instance map from RGB-D input, step by step. Vision-language models then label objects from a few chosen views, giving steady tracking and zero-shot names.
arxiv-2603-26941: Kargar builds a variational theory for the variable-exponent modulus of curve families in symmetric domains. Two shapes are treated: annuli with a radial exponent, and cylinders with an axial one. A sphere-based trick shrinks the annulus problem to one dimension. It yields a unique extremal density in closed form. A fiber trick does the same job for the cylinder. The logarithmic and constant densities return in the conformal and constant-exponent limits. Capacity and curve modulus are shown to agree for condensers.
arxiv-2603-27641: Darche and co-authors study waves crossing interfaces that change slowly in time. Each interface acts like a spring-mass link with shifting traits. Low-frequency averaging yields an effective wave equation. Bulk density and stiffness end up time-dependent yet uniform. Only the interfaces were modulated, not the bulk. Periodic modulation can open k-gaps in the spectrum. A second-order model stays reciprocal with dispersion. Time-domain simulations test both models.
arxiv-2603-27741: Chen and co-authors segment superbubbles in simulated interstellar gas. Superbubbles swell from chains of supernova blasts. Their shapes twist as they push into nearby matter. A 3D transformer model traces those shapes over time. One rich bubble serves as the demo case. Masks reveal growth patterns in fine detail. Energy retention comes into view as well. The method should transfer to other cosmic structures.
arxiv-2603-27841: Mahdian and co-authors launch Electrospinning-Data.org, a shared nanofiber data hub. Fiber traits hinge on many linked lab settings. Records today stay scattered and skew toward successes. The platform aligns with FAIR data principles. A process-structure-property model organizes each experiment. Controlled vocabulary tags keep entries machine-readable. Two-stage moderation mixes auto checks with expert review. Failure-aware records support reuse across labs.
arxiv-2603-28041: Zeleny-Mora, Gaitán-Lozano, and Martinez compute what a doublet left-right symmetric model predicts for the muon's anomalous magnetic moment. They work out all one-loop diagrams from the model's extra gauge bosons, scalars, and heavy neutrinos. Matching the measured value rules out part of the parameter space. Under equal left and right couplings, the new W boson must weigh at least 325 GeV. Letting the couplings differ pushes that bound above 1,600 GeV.
arxiv-2603-28241: Borghesani and Lamp measure how fast electrons drift through dense argon gas across wide ranges of density, temperature, and field strength. The data back a model they built earlier, which adds multiple scattering effects to classical kinetic theory. Argon's scattering cross section has an unusual energy shape. Because of that shape, none of the known multiple scattering effects can be dropped. Only the full set explains the mobility across the whole range tested.
arxiv-2603-28341: Huynh asks when the multiplicative group of a division ring can hold an abelian maximal subgroup. He proves it cannot happen for tame, finite-dimensional central division algebras over Henselian valued fields with a real valuation. The same idea rules out such subgroups in twisted Laurent series and related standard examples. He adds a malnormality test that blocks them too. Quaternion division algebras over real-closed fields fall under the ban as well.
arxiv-2603-28441: Mandal, Mukhopadhyay, and Dutta cut the cost of relativistic coupled-cluster calculations for double electron attachment. The full method chokes on heavy elements because its excitation space is huge and complex-valued. Their fix uses a frozen natural spinor basis tuned state by state, plus Cholesky-split integrals to save memory. The two-component results stay close to four-component ones. They test double ionization energies, spectra of heavy dimers, and singlet-triplet gaps of dihalocarbenes.
arxiv-2603-28741: Stoppa and Smartt present SNID-SAGE, a modern framework for supernova spectral classification and analysis. It offers both an interactive graphical interface and a scriptable command-line pipeline. The pipeline preprocesses spectra, then cross-correlates them with a curated template library using FFT methods. A composite quality metric ranks candidate matches. Redshift and classification results merge into one output with quality and confidence estimates. The template library holds about 6,000 spectra and can be upgraded. Validation used leave-one-out tests and about 46,000 WISeREP spectra.
arxiv-2603-28841: Koranga and Farooq study how CPT violation and Planck scale effects shape neutrino entanglement. They build on a CPT breaking mass matrix from flavour blind Planck scale physics. For two flavour oscillations, they compute the von Neumann entropy for neutrinos and antineutrinos apart. CPT violation leaves a gap between the two entropy curves. For a mass near 2 eV, nonzero Majorana phases are needed to match solar and KamLAND data. Those same phases set the size of the entropy gap. Entropy thus acts as a probe of Planck scale physics.
arxiv-2603-29241: D'Orsogna and co-authors study first passage times for velocity jump processes in higher dimensions. These processes move steadily, then change direction at random moments. First passage times matter in physics, biology, and finance. The team builds a framework for fixed-speed processes with varied reorientation patterns. For small mean free paths, they derive a universal formula. Two bias functions encode broad families of angular distributions. In the narrow capture limit, persistence creates unusual scaling. Simulations confirm their analytical predictions.
arxiv-2603-29441: Zheng and co-authors introduce EarthEmbeddingExplorer, a web app for searching global satellite images. Earth observation has many strong models and embedding datasets. Turning them into free, usable tools is still hard. Their app supports cross-modal queries by text, image, and location. This tutorial walks through the cloud-native design of the system. It shows how to run queries and draw insights from results. The goal is to open precomputed Earth embeddings to more researchers. The app is live online for public use.
arxiv-2603-29541: Bystrich and co-authors ask whether language model agents can identify spoken dialects like a linguist. Labeled dialect speech is scarce, which makes the task hard. Their test case is Swiss German. The agents work from phonetic transcripts made by speech recognition systems. They also get language resources like dialect feature maps and vowel history rules. With that linguistic help, the models' predictions improved. A human linguist baseline is included for comparison. The work shows transcripts can aid dialect classification.
arxiv-2603-29641: Jäckel and co-authors test ultrafast light control of spin order in the altermagnet RuO2. They fire circular light pulses, each lasting femtoseconds, at the material. Kerr measurements track how the surface spins respond. Plain ferromagnets just lose magnetization under such pulses. Here a coherent signal shows up while the pulse is on. It lasts about 200 femtoseconds in total. The team reads it as a sign of short-lived spin-polarized surface states. Those states matter for spin flow at surfaces.
arxiv-2603-29741: Allegrini and co-authors present BotVerse, a system for simulating social agents in real time. Studying bots on live networks raises ethical risks, so BotVerse keeps them in a closed setting. It still feeds agents live content drawn from Bluesky. Its engine mimics human timing and memory patterns. Researchers set up custom personas and watch multimodal exchanges at scale. A staged disinformation case shows its use for red-teaming and social science.
arxiv-2603-29841: Zimmel and Ramos set out to pin down the strong coupling from pure SU(3) gauge theory. Their route uses the decoupling strategy and a finite-volume scheme. Twisted boundary conditions keep the setup translation invariant. A gradient-flow coupling drives a step-scaling analysis. They show early results for the continuum limit of the step-scaling function. They expect smaller statistical errors than other finite-volume routes. Linear cutoff effects should also be absent.
arxiv-2603-29941: Guarino and co-authors study how to roll pixel-level uncertainty into one score per image. Segmentation tools output a score per pixel, but downstream checks need image-level values. The global average is the default, yet it ignores spatial structure. The team analyzes flaws in common aggregation strategies. They propose new ones that use spatial uncertainty patterns. Benchmarks cover out-of-distribution and failure detection on ten datasets. Spatial methods win overall, though dataset traits matter. A meta-aggregator stays robust across sets.
arxiv-2604-00041: Gangwar develops a model for drag on spherical probes moving through deep space at relativistic speeds. Adding momentum flux of baryonic and light fields yields laws exposing the Magnitude Paradox. Inertia keeps a probe's speed steady across parsec ranges, yet the boost to the matter cross-section drives fierce heating. This effect becomes large only above 0.5c and was not measured in prior Starshot-regime work. The point: deep-space drag is a heat problem, not a motion one, since the forward surface faces rates no passive matter survives.
arxiv-2604-00641: Coyette and colleagues extend the Bradley-Terry model to multiplayer games. They adapt a recent algorithm by Newman to the new model. The extension lets rankings handle contests with more than two players at once, where pairwise models fall short. The team tests the method on made-up datasets and on a real set of card games. The card-game data show the model working on genuine play records, not just simulated ones.
arxiv-2604-00841: Pesce, Farr, and de Fabritiis present AcepKa, a PlayMolecule AI tool for predicting acid dissociation constants. Those constants set protonation states, which govern solubility, permeability, and protein-ligand binding. Instead of treating each constant as one regression target, it models the full protonation set with thermodynamic consistency across linked ionization sites. Its AceConfgen conformer maker runs about 7 times faster than other GPU versions and far faster than RDKit running on many threads.
arxiv-2604-01041: Kapytka studies the hardness of inverse cellular automata on bounded-size configurations. Deciding injectivity there is co-NP-complete by Durand's theorem, and she gives a simpler proof by direct reduction from UNSAT. She shows the weak bounded arithmetic theory V0 can formalize one direction of the reduction. Since Durand's result lets inverse cellular automata on bounded configurations be viewed as propositional proofs, she proves lower bounds on their size. She uses known bounded-depth Frege bounds plus the Paris-Wilkie translation of arithmetic proofs into propositional proofs.
arxiv-2604-01841: Pham and colleagues study clinical forecasts from digital health records, hit by dimensionality, variety and skew. Tabular in-context learning and search methods do well on benchmarks, but clinic results remain unclear. The authors benchmark older, deep, and in-context learning models across scale, rarity, and transfer. PFN-based in-context models prove strong with little data but degrade under distance-based search as variety grows. They propose AWARE, using guided vectors and tools, lifting AUPRC by up to 12.2 percent in extreme imbalance.
arxiv-2604-01941: Li and colleagues build ECAC, a large benchmark for captioning daily-activity photos in early education, where generic captions miss detail. The set holds 256,121 real images with expert captions and labels, plus a Teaching Toy Recognition Score that grades professional object naming. Their hybrid trainer, RSRS, flips between reinforcement learning and supervised tuning, sending zero-reward hard cases back to supervised tuning to stop collapse. The resulting KinderMM-Cap-3B model scored 51.06 on that toy-naming measure, well ahead of rivals while keeping caption quality high.
arxiv-2604-02041: Webb and Maierhofer build a stable, fast algorithm for Hermite transforms, expansions in Hermite functions sampled at polynomial roots. The matrix splits into a diagonal part and an orthogonal matrix, allowing stable forward and inverse computation. Their method computes that split from the eigendecomposition of the Jacobi matrix. Tests show it matches or beats older stabilized methods on accuracy, runs faster, and supports use of Hermite expansions in downstream PDE work. Open source code ships with earlier methods.
arxiv-2604-02141: Zhou, Zint, Izadyar, Tao, Panozzo and Schneider make CAD meshing respect topology first. Standard pipelines approximate curved surface and curve crossings with simple pieces, often breaking adjacencies and forcing heuristic repairs. Their algorithm holds the exact boundary representation topology fixed while one user set tolerance governs geometric deviation. For any allowed tolerance the mesh stays topologically correct, with only fidelity fading as tolerance grows. Tests on thousands of real CAD models, including cases where standard tools fail, confirm the gain.
arxiv-2604-02441: Mehrfard and team present Adaptive Multi modal KalmanNet for multi sensor driving state estimation. Sensor modules learn distinct noise traits of radar, lidar and camera. A hypernetwork tunes the filter on target type, motion state and pose. A Joseph form branch, trained on error and innovation, lifts scores and tracking over the base model. It closes the gap with old Bayesian filters on real driving data.
arxiv-2604-02541: Lailey and four colleagues design a neutron loop cavity that bounces neutrons repeatedly between perfect silicon crystal blades via Bragg reflections. The device should keep about 64 percent of neutrons alive through 10,000 reflections, confining them for seconds rather than a single pass. A proposed spin-rotation measurement would beat recent sensitivity more than tenfold, and the cavity could also sharpen searches for the neutron electric dipole moment.
arxiv-2604-02841: Kobakhidze and Loomes argue that the topology of Abelian gauge theories around a Euclidean Schwarzschild black hole skews Hawking radiation. The black hole manifold holds a non-contractible 2-sphere with Euler characteristic 2, admitting closed but not exact 2-form field strengths. These are labeled by integer electric and magnetic charges. Self-dual and anti-self-dual dyonic setups carry zero Euclidean energy and fit the Schwarzschild geometry. Both classes feed the thermal equilibrium vacuum.
arxiv-2604-03041: Asambo and five colleagues map quantum-dot dynamics across timescales at low temperature with asynchronous optical sampling from a frequency comb. Standard spectroscopy cannot capture long-lived relaxation and short-lived quantum beats together, trading temporal resolution against total time. With a galvanometric scanner, they map a 1 by 1 millimeter square at 441 points in 30 minutes, work that would take over 12 days. Each location resolves both quantum beats and relaxation lifetimes, giving new insight into dot groups and enabling rapid feedback in device making.
arxiv-2604-03141: Jafari, Allan, and Iyyer argue that checking long-form model answers for truth misses half the job when only precision is scored. Their framework also measures recall against reference facts built from outside sources, weighting each fact by relevance and salience. They find current models score far better on precision than recall, covering top facts well while leaving much relevant material out.
arxiv-2604-03441: Adak and colleagues show microwave-to-optical transfer through magnon-exciton coupling in the layered antiferromagnet CrSBr. Exciting the magnet's resonance imprints coherent ripple on a bounced light probe, creating sidebands enhanced near exciton peaks. Even in a bulk crystal without cavity boost, transfer spans about 300 megahertz, pointing toward large-scale broadband quantum network links.
arxiv-2604-03841: Pardis Taghavi and colleagues distilled large vision foundation models into compact student experts using little labeled data and much unlabeled data. Their three-stage pipeline adapts the teacher by self-training, transfers knowledge through a unified multi-objective loss, and refines the student against pseudo-label bias. A pixel-wise contrastive loss keeps instances apart and aligns teacher and student embeddings. On Cityscapes and ADE20K, a student about 11 times smaller beat its zero-shot teacher by wide margins.
arxiv-2604-04141: Sho Kawano, Paul A. Parker, and Zehang Richard Li developed data thinning to validate small area estimation models. Thinning splits one observation into independent training and test parts, enabling out-of-sample validation from area figures alone, given Gaussianity and known variances. They built an unbiased estimator of thinned-data mean squared error and showed a regular gap from its full-data counterpart for the Fay-Herriot model. Simulations on American Community Survey microdata found it competitive with and more stable than information-criterion and simulation methods.
arxiv-2604-04441: Wei and Liu extend earlier work on cuspy black hole shadows, windows into strong gravity. Using parametric terms for the shadow boundary, they sort shadows by topology into rectangular and 8-shape forms. They build a gravity-thermodynamics correspondence, mapping the cuspy shadow to the swallow-tail behavior of free energy. The shadow edge's self-crossing, marking a phase transition, can be pinned down through three separate, matching thermodynamic-like routes. They derive the critical exponents for cusp rise, finding them matching the mean-field class.
arxiv-2604-04841: Chen and five colleagues tackle fake singing voices, which carry wide pitch swings and varied tone that fool detectors built for speech alone. Their system studies recordings sampled at 44.1 kilohertz, pairing a full-band view of the whole sound with specialist bands that hunt faint synthesis flaws spread unevenly across frequencies. Tested on the WildSVDD set, high-frequency bands added decisive clues, and the combined model beat detectors limited to 16 kilohertz sampling.
arxiv-2604-04941: Sun and four colleagues expose hidden algebraic structure in combinatorial optimization to shrink the search for a global optimum. Their framework finds structure, defines its rules, builds quotient spaces that merge repeats, and searches the reduced spaces. Across rule tasks such as patient subgroup discovery and molecular screening, conjunctive rules form a monoid. Through a vector encoding, they prove an isomorphism to the Boolean hypercube with bitwise OR, so logical AND in rules becomes bitwise OR in the encoding.
arxiv-2604-05141: Sitaram and six co-authors explore the Balmer decrement as a signature of inflow onto face-on galaxies. Galaxies require inflows of gas from the medium to sustain star formation over time. Yet detections of accretion onto galaxies remain very few. Studies in absorption observe limited sightlines. Emission studies struggle to distinguish inflowing gas from outflowing gas. They test the Balmer decrement, the Hα/Hβ ratio, in systems as a diagnostic for flow geometry in disk-like galaxies. They use mock observations of a Milky Way-mass galaxy.
arxiv-2604-05241: Makalic and Schmidt show that the goal splits into claim entropy and cross-entropy, weighing naming cost against coding cost. For a fixed split, each cell's point is the spread cutting gap from that cell's data spread. Under shape, optimal SMML splits approach pullbacks, through the fit gauge, of weighted Voronoi tilings, with claim chances as weights. For exp groups, SMML points satisfy a moment rule and act as KL/Bregman centroids, while cells are pullbacks of convex shapes in data space.
arxiv-2604-05441: Sun and Zhang examine two degenerate wave equations joined at a single point, with control applied at the boundary. They build estimates on weighted spaces and use frequency-domain tools to prove polynomial stability. The decay rate hinges on how deep the degeneracy runs, linking boundary control to that depth.
arxiv-2604-05541: Wang and ten colleagues build EchoAgent, an agent that reads echocardiograms end to end like a cardiac sonographer. It absorbs guideline knowledge into a structured base, parses video streams, identifies views, segments anatomy, and measures quantities, then reasons over the combined evidence. Tests across 48 views and 14 heart regions put it at the top on structure analyses, at up to 80 percent overall accuracy.
arxiv-2604-05641: Ambjørn and Loll present causal dynamical triangulations, a lattice route to quantum gravity that sums over triangulated spacetimes built from flat Minkowskian blocks. Simulations show a quantum universe emerging near the Planck scale with de Sitter-like global shape and a short-scale spectral dimension near 2. Signs of an ultraviolet fixed point point toward a nontrivial continuum theory.
arxiv-2604-06241: Taylor and three colleagues argue agentic coding tools need a stricter boundary before running code. AI IDEs and agents compress discovery, fetching, opening, installation, and execution into one opaque loop, leaving the execution choice implicit. Their Rust system ZitPit turns first-seen artifacts into lasting policy records that must precede any execution rights on protected hosts. Evidence is narrow: Git intake tests show approved items fetching faster than unmanaged downloads, plus session and egress proofs. It unifies admission, repo state, capability-scoped execution, and durable records at the boundary.
arxiv-2604-06441: Sadhukhan, Tsirkin, Zhumagulov, and Mazin study how anomalous Hall conductivity, a sideways voltage in magnetic metals, depends on magnetization in weak itinerant ferromagnet ZrZn2. The anomalous Hall effect long lacked an account, and belief tied it in a straight line to net magnetization. Karplus and Luttinger explained it via spin-orbit coupling and Berry curvature, yet only for exchange coupling weaker than that coupling. In single-domain ZrZn2, calculation shows the linear link holds near zero magnetization but breaks down and flips sign at about 0.4 Bohr magnetons per zirconium.
arxiv-2604-06541: Gurkanli and Spannowsky test a multiscale tensor-network design. Jets arise from a branching cascade spanning angular and momentum scales. Their MERA-inspired autoencoder acts on ordered jet constituents. They compare it with a dense autoencoder, the tree limit, and baselines. Two questions guide the work: whether compression fits the data, and whether MERA disentanglers beat trees. Benchmarks and an ablation show the multiscale structure fits jet data well. MERA disentanglers help most at strong bottlenecks. The study supports hierarchical compression for jets.
arxiv-2604-06841: Li and four colleagues give neural-network quantum states spin symmetry. Usual fermionic designs ignore this symmetry and can land on tainted spin states with wrong energies. Their SA-NNBF ansatz pairs orbitals that shift with layout plus a packed spin eigenfunction. A tensor squeeze plus a particle-hole form make Monte Carlo runs doable past 100 electrons. Tests on hydrogen chains and iron-sulfur clusters end taint and beat plain backflow energies, and on FeMoco the method rivals spin-adapted DMRG at bond dimension 10,000 with far fewer parameters.
arxiv-2604-06941: Sultana and Chattopadhyay test an exponential quintessence model against cosmic clocks, baryon acoustic waves, and supernova data. With a Monte Carlo fit, the data tighten bounds on the model numbers. Values for expansion rate, distance modulus, and distance track data closely and follow the standard baseline. Information-criterion comparison finds the model statistically comparable to the standard model despite extra numbers. It reproduces the shift from matter domination to acceleration, keeps the equation of state above minus one, and gives an age matching Planck 2018.
arxiv-2604-07341: Ibrahimzada and three colleagues present ReCodeAgent, an autonomous multi-agent system for translating whole code repositories between programming languages and validating the results. Users supply only the source project and target language, and agents use each language's own analysis tools to translate and check the code. Tested on 118 real projects across six languages, it beats four prior neuro-symbolic and agentic methods, lifting ground-truth test pass rates by 60.8 percent at an average cost of 15.30 dollars. Multi-agent design matters: a single agent drops pass rates by 40.4 percent.
arxiv-2604-07441: Chung and 12 colleagues test the tip of the red giant branch as a cosmic distance marker under varied stellar populations. Using synthetic color-magnitude diagrams in two infrared bands, they vary metallicity, alpha-element enhancement, age, and helium. Metallicity and alpha enhancement dominate the tip brightness, while age matters little and helium barely matters. Mixed populations under typical halo conditions shift the tip by under 0.028 magnitudes in the I band, well inside reported systematic errors. The tip thus stays a sturdy distance anchor for precision cosmology.
arxiv-2604-07541: Buys proves simple-graph analogues of Brown and Colbourn's results on reliability roots. For connected multigraphs, complex reliability-polynomial roots are dense in the unit disk, and real-root closure is minus one to zero plus one. Buys confirms a recent Brown-McMullin conjecture by proving both analogues for simple graphs. The proof uses graphs formed by substituting each edge of a cycle with a complete graph, relying on asymptotic behavior of reliability and split-reliability polynomials of complete graphs.
arxiv-2604-07741: Wei and five colleagues build a deepfake detector that checks sound and video together for mismatches between the two streams. Their multi-scale cross-modal transformer, MSCT, blends nearby features with multi-scale self-attention and fuses the two streams with a differential cross-modal attention step. The design targets weak feature extraction and drift between streams in older detectors, and it posts competitive scores on the FakeAVCeleb test set.
arxiv-2604-07841: Datta studies how classical chaos shapes quantum tunneling in driven nonlinear systems. Phase-space shapes steer purely quantum transport, and the paper spells out how. Under driving and random kicks, tunneling rates take a triggered form set by real classical barriers. Chaos-assisted tunneling and its coherent destruction then appear as close cousins, both rooted in the same driving-induced reshaping and interference. The result unifies control of tunneling in non-integrable systems.
arxiv-2604-08541: Xu and nine colleagues name a failure mode in multimodal mixture of experts models: seeing but not thinking. Models read images correctly yet fail reasoning that the same problem in pure text passes, because visual inputs route differently in middle layers where domain experts cluster. A routing guided intervention that boosts domain expert activation lifts complex visual reasoning by up to 3.17 percent across three models and six benchmarks, and the gains transfer across tasks.
arxiv-2604-08941: Sadanandan and Behzadan ask whether one score can flag two failures in medical vision-language models answering yes-or-no questions about chest X-rays. The failures are confident mistakes, and answers that flip when the same question is rephrased. On the MedGemma model they test single-pass predictive entropy, a measure of model uncertainty, across two hospital datasets. At a 5 percent risk target, one forward pass answers 88.5 percent of cases, matching heavier methods. Yet even a model 91 percent accurate contradicts itself on 13 percent of items under rephrasing.
arxiv-2604-09041: Cachay, Watson-Parris, and Yu show that frontier probabilistic weather forecasting needs neither specialized architectures nor massive budgets. Current leading models rival physics-based ensembles but demand custom designs and heavy compute, raising the barrier to entry. Their U-Cast forecaster uses a standard U-Net backbone with a recipe: deterministic pretraining on mean absolute error, then brief probabilistic fine-tuning. It trains in under 12 H200 GPU-days and produces a 15-day ensemble forecast in 3 seconds, cutting compute and latency over tenfold against diffusion-based models.
arxiv-2604-09341: Ferraro, Naves, and Larson analyze Fock-state lattices from an algebra view, starting from a Lie algebra. Cartan parts define lattice sites, while root parts set bonds. That links algebra structure to size, links, balance constraints, transport, and revival effects. Looking at common Lie algebras, they find linked grids and Lie phase spaces, linking lattice motion to phase-space shape, though not every tame model admits such an algebra.
arxiv-2604-09441: Tomizawa studies smooth maps on closed manifolds of at least three dimensions. Two hyperbolic periodic points link in a heteroclinic cycle there, with one transverse link and one not. Near such a map, open sets of nearby maps hold infinitely many attracting periodic circles. The circles are normally hyperbolic. His proof reduces the motion to the standard Hénon map and corrects a formula for its Lyapunov coefficient.
arxiv-2604-10141: Mangeolle and Knolle build a quantum theory of Sondheimer oscillations in thin films under strong magnetic fields. These resistance oscillations come from the match between cyclotron motion and film thickness, long seen as a size effect. Their theory shows band topology shifts the oscillation frequency. That contrasts with Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations, where topology shows only in the phase. Quantum Sondheimer oscillations thus probe the full Landau level spectrum head-on. A simple model with tunable Berry phase shows how topology appears in measurable spectra, with surface-roughness damping.
arxiv-2604-10341: Liu and three colleagues build VeriTrans, a trust-first system turning natural-language needs into solver-ready logic with checker-gated trust. Its flow joins a trained tool, round-trip rebuild as a pass gate, and standard build, all under fixed setup with per-item logging for audits and replay fixes. On SatBench with 2,100 specs, it reaches 94.46 percent SAT/UNSAT scores, with median round-trip likeness about 88 percent. Compact fine-tuning on 100 to 150 curated cases lifts truth by about 1 to 2 points without raising latency.
arxiv-2604-10641: Razeghi asks how many synthetic face identities can truly be told apart under one verification rule. A generator's raw count is too high. He defines capacity as the largest set of latent identity codes whose embeddings meet acceptance and non-match constraints. For fixed pipelines this equals a spherical-code count over realizable embeddings. For random embeddings he derives separation rules, lower bounds, and zero-error conditions, and tests the sampled version on a DigiFace-1M subset under three recognizers.
arxiv-2604-10941: Liu presents a generative frame for direct-to-chip cooling channels for NVIDIA's GB200 Superchip, where rising AI workloads raise power densities and heuristic layouts miss non-uniform temperatures. A finite-difference model gives fast temperature predictions and feeds feedback to a reaction-diffusion process generating channel topologies under constraints. Iterating generation and evaluation shifts cooling toward high-power regions, curbing hot spots. Against baseline, the channels cut average temperature by over 5 degrees and maximum temperature by over 35 degrees. Generative design plus lightweight modeling can boost direct-to-chip cooling.
arxiv-2604-11341: Lierse, Moghaddam, and Werner replace rigid per-interval emission rates with time-bound emissions budgets for applications facing carbon pricing. Budgets let software save unused allowances when grid carbon intensity is low and spend them when it is high. A MAPE-K feedback loop watches power use and grid intensity and adapts via scaling or migration. Simulations on six weeks of data from Germany, France, and Poland improved task fulfillment up to 36 percent in variable grids, with parity in stable grids.
arxiv-2604-11541: Bose and Faryad systematically test a variational quantum classifier under combined classical and quantum noise, using the Titanic dataset. Classical noise models, from speckle and impulse noise to quantization and feature dropout, precede quantum encoding via a ZZ feature map. Depolarizing, damping, Pauli, and readout errors enter at the circuit level. Classical input noise sharply worsens decoherence, destabilizing training and cutting accuracy. Pipelines must therefore be designed and judged with both noise sources in mind.
arxiv-2604-12541: Jean Fasel and William Hornslien write down explicit polynomial forms of a suspended Hopf map. The map is defined over the integers, using motivic homotopy theory. From this work they derive an explicit rank 2 vector bundle. The bundle lives on the Jouanolou device of three-dimensional projective space over the integers. The work links abstract homotopy work to concrete geometric objects. Such forms make abstract maps tangible for further study.
arxiv-2604-12841: Christopher Chamberland and four colleagues decode surface codes fast with an AI pre-decoder. Real-time fault-tolerant computing needs block-wise parallel decoding. A local parallel pre-decoder clears most errors before a global decoder finishes. The design works with any global decoder and is fully open source. With PyMatching, runtimes reach about one microsecond per round at large distances. Logical error rates fall versus global decoding alone. A noise-learning module infers weights from syndrome data alone, nearly matching PyMatching.
arxiv-2604-13041: Zhang and Yang build TableNet, a large table-structure dataset produced by an autonomous multi-agent system powered by language models. The generator blends visual, structural, and semantic controls to synthesize varied, annotated tables in any style or domain. A diversity-based active learning recognizer then learns from the most informative samples, cutting training data sharply while beating models trained on dominant table datasets on real web tables.
arxiv-2604-13241: Kowalczyk and Kowalski forecast learner satisfaction early in massive open online courses, when intervention is still possible. Most methods infer it only after the course from reviews and ratings. Their TET-LLM framework fuses a temporal event Transformer over behavioral sequences, language-model embeddings from early forum posts and feedback, and short-text topic distributions. At the 7-day horizon it reaches RMSE of 0.82 and AUC of 0.77, beating aggregate-feature and text-only baselines, with near-nominal 90 percent interval coverage.
arxiv-2604-13341: Flores gives a geometric reading of Newton's fast rule for Bayesian mixture estimation, a field where old Markov chain Monte Carlo methods cost too much. Newton's rule gave a fast alternative, but its Bayes link was only half clear. Flores shows the rule moves step by step like a gradient flow over chance distributions under Fisher-Rao geometry, in short a slope descent in distribution space. That view clears up convergence, links the rule to variational Bayes, and points to new rules made by changing the geometry or discretization.
arxiv-2604-14141: Chen and eleven colleagues present LingBot-Map, a feed-forward foundation model that rebuilds scenes from streaming video with geometric accuracy and temporal consistency. Its geometric context transformer joins three aids: an anchor context, a window tied to poses, and a memory of the path. Together they ground coordinates, gather dense cues, and correct long-range drift. The compact streaming state supports stable inference near 20 frames per second on 518 by 378 inputs over sequences beyond 10,000 frames, beating streaming and iterative rivals across benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-14341: Fu and sixty colleagues report EP250302a, a GRB-like flash found in soft X-rays by the Einstein Probe at a redshift of 1.131, with follow-up from X-rays to radio. A sharp X-ray flare plus later rebrightening defies a lone afterglow picture and points to several ejecta parts. The team reads the flare as a late shell smashing into the slowed leading blast wave, lighting both flare and rebrightening. Such a late shell could come from a second burst of central-engine activity.
arxiv-2604-14641: Huang, Liu, He, and Gilpin ask whether teaching models to draw layouts from spatial descriptions can instill spatial understanding, as sketching does. Text2Space pairs descriptions with ASCII grid layouts from ground truth and spatial question-answer pairs, separating building failures from reasoning failures. Evaluation finds a Read-Write Asymmetry: models read ASCII well but struggle to produce it, and construction errors corrupt later answers. Layout-construction training improves spatial reasoning from text alone, even with no ASCII at inference. Adding comprehension training amplifies gains transferring to three external benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-14941: Garg, Mittal, and Gupta present Text2Arch, a dataset for generating scientific architecture diagrams from natural language descriptions. No clean large-scale open-access dataset exists for the task, leaving no effective open models. Text2Arch pairs scientific architecture images with textual descriptions and DOT code representations. Fine-tuned small language models on the dataset beat DiagramAgent and match GPT-4o in-context generations. Code, data, and models are publicly available.
arxiv-2604-15241: Dror and Kyriazis assess whether global cosmic strings leave a detectable particle signature. Gauge-symmetry strings decay mainly into gravitational waves, but global-symmetry strings decay into Nambu-Goldstone bosons that may persist as dark matter or dark radiation. Using semi-numerical estimates of energy density and the matter power spectrum, they compare predictions against microwave background, Lyman-alpha forest, large-scale structure, and UV luminosity data. The comparison yields constraints on the boson mass.
arxiv-2604-15541: Betancur, Castrillón, and Zapata probe inelastic sub-GeV dark matter at DUNE's near detector, where a dark Higgs mechanism splits a Dirac fermion into two Majorana states. New annihilation channels through the dark Higgs open parameter space matching the observed relic abundance. The near liquid-argon detector can probe those regions, especially where large dark-photon-to-dark-matter mass ratios blunt decay-based searches.
arxiv-2604-15641: Zhang, Chakraborti, and Reiter offer Half-Moon Cookie, a private blocklist. A user tests an item near a firm's secret list in a metric space, with neither side seeing the other's goods. The build splits the map step from the list check, so each uses its own private, fast method. A cheap re-check proves an item passed before, letting receivers trust a first pass and blocking time-of-check tricks. The same build fits look-alike malware spotting, blocking bad code with no leaks.
arxiv-2604-15841: Dianqing Lin and nine colleagues introduce Mouse, a benchmark that tests large language models on Chouxiang, a subcultural style of Chinese internet language, across six tasks. Current leading models show clear limits on several tasks while doing well where contextual meaning matters most. The paper also examines why performance lags, whether model-based judging matches human judgment on translation, and what drives translation quality, aiming to spur research on evolving online language.
arxiv-2604-15941: Watanabe and Umetani propose neural Gabor splatting, an upgrade to 3D Gaussian splatting for sharp color detail on surfaces. Standard splatting needs many primitives for high-frequency scenes, since each primitive holds only one color. Their method equips each primitive with a small multi-layer perceptron that models wide color shifts inside one primitive. A frequency-aware densification step prunes and clones primitives by frequency energy, keeping counts in check. Tests on standard benchmarks, including checkered patterns, show accurate rebuilds of tricky sharp-detail scenes.
arxiv-2604-16041: Bottazzi and Varela study when an n-by-n Hermitian matrix is minimal with respect to a C-star-subalgebra in the spectral norm. They broaden the moment of a subspace and relate it to the joint numerical range and subdifferentials of the maximum eigenvalue. They extend results known for diagonal operators and describe the subdifferential of the maximum eigenvalue via the moment of the matching eigenspace. They also describe minimality via moments and subdifferentials, with examples.
arxiv-2604-16141: Lu studies how few generators a generalised wreath product of symmetric groups needs, building the product over a finite ordered index set. Each factor permutes its own set, and the construction links them through the ordering. The paper determines the smallest number of generators required, giving a clean count for this family of permutation groups.
arxiv-2604-16341: Frizzo and eight co-authors benchmark deep learning for virtual reality user identification. Motion data acts as a behavioural biometric for secure access. Modern architectures remain largely untested on VR motion data. This holds especially for state space models. Earlier studies report identification accuracies above 94 percent. Using the Who is Alyx dataset from 71 users playing Half-Life: Alyx, they compare LSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, Transformer, and state space models on time series motion data. Their work gives the first comprehensive benchmark for VR user identification.
arxiv-2604-16441: Cha, Chun and Park present iPhoneme, a brain-to-text system for people with ALS-related speech loss. It pairs a ConformerXL phoneme decoder with a gaze-assisted input design that avoids dwell-time selection, using combined gaze and silent speech instead. Tested on intracranial recordings from speech motor cortex, the system reached about 92 percent phoneme accuracy with a language model and beam search. Running on an ordinary processor with low latency, it offers a practical route to real-time communication for users who cannot speak.
arxiv-2604-16741: Wang and Steinfeld explore group-based models for robot navigation in crowded walker scenes. Pedestrian groups make robot driving safer and more social, yet prior work used limited cases or noise-prone outside spotting modules. Group guessing score affects driving performance only barely in crowded environments. The authors propose a visible edge-based group representation, built into a driving tool with a simple group model. Sims show matching safety and grace in dense crowds with faster computation, and a real-robot rollout shows real gains.
arxiv-2604-16841: Chen and colleagues propose EFDiff, an Earth foundation model-guided diffusion framework for land surface temperature super-resolution. Coarse thermal observations badly starve fine-scale structure, making zoom hard. Prithvi-EO-2.0 encodes sharp multi-band shine into geospatial embeddings fed via cross-focus. Two variants trade look realism against pixel-level truth, and the tool beats baselines under an extreme 32 times scale gap. Cross-focus guiding beats channel stacking, and the tool spreads to remote sensing problems with ready geo maps.
arxiv-2604-16941: Dao and five colleagues build MEMRES, an agent-style resolver for Python dependency failures that tries remembered fixes and a curated map of imports to packages before asking a language model. Tested on 2,890 code snippets, it resolves 2,503 of them, about 87 percent, well above the 54.7 percent reported for the earlier PLLM system.
arxiv-2604-17041: Zhao, Lou, and Zheng protect vision-language models from unauthorized reuse with fingerprints that stay inside normal semantics. Older marks rely on odd queries or out-of-distribution responses, which their Semantic Divergence Attack exposes by filtering suspect queries against a reference model. Their SIF framework moves text watermark signals into images and hardens them against worst-case perturbations, staying stealthy and robust under fine-tuning and quantization.
arxiv-2604-17241: Wang and five colleagues present GaLa, a vision-language system for step-by-step planning in robots. It models object items as nodes in a graph, with region-level links grouping objects by traits and use-based meaning, showing hidden links and the ranking of use-based regions. A TriView HyperGraph Encoder keeps meaning match across node, area, and node-area link views via contrast learning, feeding graph meaning into downstream vision-language thinking. On ActPlan1K and ALFRED, GaLa beats methods on task success rate, LCS, and planning scores.
arxiv-2604-17541: Wu and Ou-Yang work out when charged colloidal crystals lose acoustic stability as electrostatic forces soften them. A uniform softening acting on a direction-dependent elastic background weakens sound waves most along certain crystal axes. The paper gives a complete long-wave stability rule for cubic crystals, with closed-form critical couplings for the [100], [110], and [111] directions. A small-scale derivation from Poisson-Boltzmann theory in a spherical cell then ties the coupling constant to salt concentration, particle charge, and volume fraction.
arxiv-2604-17641: Vylet, Huang, and Balents study a low-energy Kondo model on the triangular lattice, with electrons in a Gamma pocket and three pockets at the M points. Its Fermi-surface nesting favors triple-Q order from band structure alone. Treating local moments as spins on a four-sublattice cell, they find non-coplanar regions, including tetrahedral and canted states, plus ferromagnetic and coplanar phases. Chiral phases stay stable across coupling ranges and under field, and some host a quantum anomalous Hall state at conductivity 4 e squared over h.
arxiv-2604-18141: Ruiz-Guirola, Filippou, and Lopez design a thrifty geofencing system for camera sensors around a protected site. The sensors harvest energy, so frequent wake-ups would drain their tiny stores. A central access point therefore schedules sensing, sleeping, and reporting based on each device's viewing angle and range. Reinforcement learning picks placements that spot intruders sooner than even grid layouts while using fewer devices.
arxiv-2604-18541: Mas, Terzioglu, and Ipsen highlight the Fourier transform's key role in finding inversion formulas for integral transforms in tomographic imaging. They show the principle by working out reverse rules, first for the divergent beam transform, then for the V-line transform. That V-line transform arises in current models of single-scattering optical tomography, showing how one transform method serves distinct imaging shapes.
arxiv-2604-18641: Arshad and three colleagues show a Weyl-flat null start for inflation need not clash with readings. In single-field inflation, any past with epsilon tending to a limit between zero and one as N grows ends up power-law. A tweak, power above one, keeps the far-past shape, gives an exit, and yields finite-N behavior. In e-fold time, scalar and tensor laws give a band: the spectral index sits in the Planck range, and the tensor-to-scalar ratio runs near a thousandth to hundredth.
arxiv-2604-18741: Ramesh and four colleagues study how older adults with multiple chronic conditions track health data using physical tokens as input visualizations. Collecting data alone rarely yields insight, since reflection usually waits until records are reviewed later. In interview and diary studies over two weeks, participants adapted the tokens to their own needs, folded them into daily routines, and used tangible markers to spot patterns. The paper closes with design guidance for tools that support tracking, expression, and meaningful reflection.
arxiv-2604-18841: Miller and Lee introduce QuIC, a training free quantum graph embedding that maps graphs to sorted outputs through a fixed parameterized circuit. In the ideal one repetition setting, the sorted output is permutation invariant and injective on labeled graphs under an irrational angle condition. The authors then test how much of this holds up under finite shot estimation, truncation, noise, transpilation, and hardware execution. A hardware study of 14,800 transpiled circuits across 37 CFI families on IBM Heron reports separation up to 66 qubits.
arxiv-2604-19141: Schusterbauer and five colleagues explore patch noise scales: some regions denoise, others need refinement. Naive variation across tokens performs poorly, exposing training states absent at inference. They introduce a sampler capping patch information during training; patch timesteps beat standard baselines. A patch difficulty head enables samplers allocating compute where needed. With noise varying over space and time, Patch Forcing advances easier regions first to provide context for harder ones. Patch Forcing beats baselines on ImageNet and scales to text-guided synthesis.
arxiv-2604-19641: Hoang, Wang, Zerrouki, and Delahaye introduce Regulation Zero 2, a step-by-step planning tool for early-stage air traffic flow work that works in rule space. It answers rule cascading, where interacting traffic rules compound in nonlinear, hard-to-predict ways and strain a network operator's ability to protect sectors reliably. The tool tunes ordered sets of flow-level rules that stay compatible as far as possible, as rising demand meets persistent staffing shortages.
arxiv-2604-20041: Chen and four colleagues advance normalizing flows, a family of generative models, with iterative TARFlow, or iTARFlow. Unlike diffusion models, training stays fully end-to-end and likelihood-based. Sampling runs one step at a time, then applies step-by-step denoising in the diffusion style. The model does well across ImageNet sizes of 64, 128, and 256 pixels, and the authors also analyze its artifacts to guide future work.
arxiv-2604-20241: Foppiano and five colleagues build an author-centered knowledge graph of battery research from OpenAlex, a large open catalog of papers. Each author gets a weighted descriptor vector mixing broad OpenAlex concepts with fine title and abstract keyphrases, pulled by KeyBERT with ChatGPT behind it. Vector weights reflect descriptor source, author spot, and recency, and the graph covers 189,581 battery works. The vectors back author similarity scores, group finding, and browser search, and the graph ships in RDF linked to Wikidata, so it plugs into outside linked data.
arxiv-2604-20541: Groisman proves the octopus picture for basins of attraction in multistable systems, for phase oscillators linked in a cycle. Equilibria are indexed by a winding number, and basin volumes follow a Gaussian law in that number. A distance from a sample to its attractor, scaled by size's square root, concentrates near 1.814 overall. Along almost every line through a twisted state, the ray enters other basins infinitely often, with frequencies set by basin volumes. The inscribed ball radius and first-exit distance follow formulas that show an anisotropic head.
arxiv-2604-20641: Franco, Couto, Vasconcelos, and Santos study how picks that combine opinion likeness and network likeness shape splits. Link picks suggest links, driven by triadic closure through mutual friends and sameness through traits. Both lead to split states, but differ: opinion likeness raises spread, while network likeness creates more broken parts and split networks leaning to one opinion. Under sameness, adding a weak lean on network likeness prevents splitting and favors middle views. The work can guide pick design for linked forces, helping middle views live together even in splitting settings.
arxiv-2604-20741: Brown gives a higher-dimensional irrationality criterion for periods given as Mellin integrals with many inputs. It is an upper bound on the multivariate transfinite diameter of the image of the domain under the Mellin inputs. As a proof, he shows the approach with work for a 5-parameter family for zeta(2) over the genus-0 moduli space with five marked points. That proves the irrationality of zeta(2) in higher dimensions, based on an upper bound on a transfinite diameter of that moduli space.
arxiv-2604-20841: Kim, Kim, Cho, Lee, and Joo present DeVI, a system that learns physics-based character control for dexterous human-object interaction by copying text-conditioned synthetic videos. To handle unreliable 3D object motion rebuild, they build hybrid imitation targets that mix rebuilt 3D human motion with tracked 2D object paths. Their Visual HOI Alignment further tunes the human reference to match the made video and the starting 3D object setup. Tests show the hybrid form beats baselines and that Visual HOI Alignment lifts imitation success.
arxiv-2604-20941: Chatterjee turns symbolic regression, a search for short formulas, onto the GWTC-4 catalog of binary black hole mergers. Phenomenological models had traced patterns in that catalog, but with little clarity about which laws were real. He pulls out compact closed-form laws for how merger rates shift with redshift, how spin links to mass ratio, and how mass ratios spread near the 10 and 35 solar-mass peaks. The laws show spin links are set by widening spreads, not by shifting means.
arxiv-2604-21041: Aladawi, Alam, and Karray harden image diffusion unlearning against concept revival, in which erased concepts return when a model is fine-tuned. They adapt Projected Gradient Unlearning post-hoc. A Core Gradient Space built from retain concepts lets gradient updates be projected into its complement, so fine-tuning cannot undo erasure. It eliminates revival for style concepts and slows it for object concepts, taking roughly 6 minutes against about 2 hours for Meta-Unlearning. It complements Meta-Unlearning, and retain-concept choice is best guided by visual similarity over semantic grouping.
arxiv-2604-21441: Lukas Müllender, Berk Hess, and Erik Lindahl connect neural network potentials to GROMACS for hybrid machine-learning/molecular-mechanics simulation. Their interface lets PyTorch-trained potentials supply energies and forces for chosen subsets or whole systems, open to descriptor-based or message-passing designs. It plugs into GROMACS sampling and free-energy workflows. Demos cover peptide torsional landscapes, solvation free energies, and protein-ligand systems, with water-box benchmarks across designs.
arxiv-2604-22041: Zhang and four colleagues say test plans need their own verification checks to catch slips like mixed-in factors. Cause and effect, what world actions leading to results means, had not yet been put on firm code-proof footing. The authors study d-separation, a classic graph rule for when experiment plans control enough mixed-in factors. Their main Rocq-checked result: d-separation matches a new semantic definition from security non-mixing.
arxiv-2604-22141: Iwao, Motegi and Ohkawa study 3D partition functions built from a tetrahedral L-operator. Such functions count weighted states in models of matter. Where the deformation parameter q equals zero, they write a class of these functions as tensor Schur polynomials, products of classical symmetric polynomials. From that form they get a shuffle formula and one shared form for two known identities. They also treat general q, giving explicit deformed versions of elementary symmetric functions. The machinery also applies to a multispecies exclusion process.
arxiv-2604-22741: Kempton and colleagues describe swdatatoolkit, a Python library for fetching, tidying, and working with solar and space-weather data. It joins downloads from sun-science sources with image clean-up, edge finding, texture measures, magnetic-field work, and solar values. Its modular build backs work that others can repeat, for first looks and for machine-learning studies.
arxiv-2604-22941: Valette proves a Sobolev embedding theorem for Borel measures with a globally subanalytic density function. Given such a measure on a set and a globally subanalytic mapping into a bounded open set, he derives an embedding for the associated Sobolev space of the push-forward measure. It lands in the space of inner Lipschitz functions. The paper also gives an application to kernel theory. A Sobolev embedding, in this setting, relates functions with controlled derivatives to functions with stronger regularity or boundedness properties.
arxiv-2604-23041: Moseley, Teyssier, and Abel present Itô tracers, continuous-time Lagrangian particles for Eulerian hydrodynamics whose moments match gas advection, diffusion, and dispersion. Old tracers carried by cell speeds miss code diffusion and show steady bias, while Monte Carlo tracers jump between cells and break paths. A subgrid variant swaps code diffusion for a Smagorinsky-Lilly eddy diffusivity. In flow and turbulence tests, Itô tracers largely match or beat Monte Carlo scores and improve tracer-gas links there.
arxiv-2604-23241: Zaman and Unoki tackle human-imitated speech forgery, which fools people and detectors more easily than AI-made speech because it sounds natural. They propose a Spectro-Temporal Modulation frame built on hearing, using Gammatone and Gammachirp cochlear filterbanks to capture joint time and frequency shifts. A Segmental-STM variant studies short overlapping windows for fine-grained time detail. Tests show STM near human scores, while Segmental-STM beats them, backing hearing-inspired models for voice checks.
arxiv-2604-23441: Makos and colleagues find a third quantum pathway in attosecond interferometry of carbon dioxide, one that textbook accounts miss. A near-infrared pulse acts not only on the freed electron but also on the ion left behind. That extra action changes the strength and phase of the interference sidebands for specific breakup channels. Comparing angle- and energy-resolved measurements with theory lets the team isolate each pathway's share.
arxiv-2604-23641: Yan introduces VDLF-Net, a vision network that adds a small variational autoencoder to a multi-scale convolutional backbone for adaptive and few-shot learning. Latent vectors and a softmax gate steer the backbone's feature maps, while normalised embeddings from the gated maps feed the classifier. It beats known baselines on standard tests, and tests that drop parts show the fine-resolution scale matters most.
arxiv-2604-23841: Hoss, Link, and Klarmann solve job-shop scheduling with a unified graph framework that projects distinct node roles into one shared space. This lets a standard homogeneous graph network capture resource contention at linear cost, fixing the quadratic bottleneck of earlier models. Tests show top performance with strong zero-shot transfer. The job-to-machine ratio drives success most, and training at the saturation point where jobs match machines yields scale-free strategies.
arxiv-2604-24541: López-March and three colleagues map how physical noise corrupts analog computing with programmable light circuits, where the basic unit, the anbit, is carried by continuous optical waves. They model noise as random photocurrent fluctuations, project it onto a geometric sphere representation, and derive a distinct noise map for each source. Tests on a fabricated silicon chip confirm the predictions and point to design rules for sturdier optical computing.
arxiv-2604-24741: Saha, Kethepalli, Guiselin, De Nardis and Sadhu uncover a shared pattern in long-time, large-scale statistics for a one-dimensional hard-rod gas. Two very different small-scale dynamics give the same non-Gaussian fluctuations for tracer positions at one time. One is stochastic diffusive motion. The other is unitary ballistic motion. The match holds up to a simple dynamical scaling. This shared pattern holds in both annealed and quenched ensembles, showing a lasting memory of the initial state. Differences appear only in multi-time statistics.
arxiv-2604-24841: Moretti, Nierste, Reeck and Steinhauser calculate QCD corrections to meson lifetime ratios. Decay widths expand in inverse mass and the strong coupling. Splittings are dominated by terms suppressed by the inverse cube of mass. They calculate three-loop contributions to B-plus, D-plus and D-s-plus ratios in symmetry limits. New corrections to Cabibbo-suppressed terms in the B ratio are also given. With sum-rule matrix elements, the B-plus to B-d-zero ratio is 1.072 with stated uncertainty. It agrees well with experimental data.
arxiv-2604-25041: Womack constructs string backgrounds in dimension 2 connecting the Hamilton cigar to the round sphere. He builds a family with one parameter of rotationally symmetric steady gradient Ricci-Yang-Mills solitons on surfaces. At one end sits the Hamilton cigar; below zero, solitons are asymptotic to cylinders. At zero sits a complete noncompact soliton with a cusp at infinity. As the parameter grows large, the family approaches a round point. He shows every complete steady gradient soliton on a surface belongs to this family.
arxiv-2604-25141: Zhang and four colleagues offer a new route to nonreciprocal unconventional magnon blockade. Their hybrid setup joins two microwave cavities to one yttrium iron garnet sphere. Nonlinear links between pump and signal cavities, plus dispersive coupling of three bosonic modes, tie pump cavity modes to magnon modes, while Kerr nonlinearity acts in the pump cavity. Weak parametric driving of the pump then yields the blockade, a step toward preparing single magnons for quantum information work.
arxiv-2604-25341: Cambie and Chang settle two open items from Filipovski and colleagues, pinning down how lopsided a graph can look under two rival measures. For general graphs the worst ratio grows like the size to the two and a half power, while for trees the cap is far tighter, just two below the size. On trees, the Albertson unevenness score also caps the order scaled graph variance, tying the two ideas together.
arxiv-2604-25441: Menta seeks an intervention lifting a non-Indic base to commercial-class Indic speech, with no new decoder. He joins three pieces: BUPS romanises seven Indic scripts to ISO-15919 for Chatterbox's Latin tokeniser. Second, a LoRA adapter on only the text-token predictor. Third, a voice-prompt recipe with a same-language clip and sampling overrides, dubbed Config B, recovers commercial sound. On Hindi, Chatterbox plus Config B replaces the accuracy-hurting LoRA. On pilot sets, Praxy Voice matches commercial baselines. Telugu retroflex collapse of 26.7 percent beats Sarvam Bulbul.
arxiv-2604-25541: Schwarzbach reports HYMN notes on cross-tech ranging for indoor-outdoor robot navigation. Mobile robots moving indoors and outdoors struggle to stay placed. Satellite and terrestrial ranging work well at home, but joining them at raw level gets little notice, and the building edge is where both degrade. HYMN syncs GNSS, Ultra-Wideband, WiFi FTM, and Bluetooth BLE data against millimeter-level ground truth. Per-zone availability and ranging residuals are mapped. The two tech classes match well, and weaknesses overlap at the indoor-outdoor switch. The dataset is public.
arxiv-2604-25741: Schölch and three colleagues identify young stars in the Bridge linking the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, using Gaia DR3 data and machine learning. The Bridge likely formed in the Clouds' most recent interaction. Some Bridge stars formed in place from stripped gas, while others may have been drawn out of the Small Cloud. A dimensionality-reduction step builds a training sample, and a neural network then classifies sources between the Clouds. The new sample spans about 15 kiloparsecs, with stars moving from the Small Cloud toward the Large Cloud.
arxiv-2604-25841: Bergougnoux, Chekan, and Kratsch study problems parameterized by multi-clique-width. Each vertex may hold several labels at once under this parameter. It generalizes clique-width and treewidth without exponential blow-up. Yet graphs of multi-clique-width k can have clique-width exponential in k. Under the Exponential Time Hypothesis, Max Cut resists the stated time on such graphs. It is the first problem whose tight times differ across the two parameters. Hamiltonian Cycle and Edge Dominating Set instead match clique-width times.
arxiv-2604-26141: Bianchi, Donà, and Muiño derive a general formula for the typical entanglement entropy of a subsystem in a many-body system with fixed global charge. At leading and subleading order in the thermodynamic limit, the entropy reduces to a single quantity: the local thermal entropy at fixed charge density. The formula covers both abelian and non-abelian symmetry, including local spaces transforming under general reducible representations. The authors illustrate it with model systems while discussing its value as a probe of quantum chaos in physical Hamiltonians.
arxiv-2604-26541: Garny, Niedermann, and Sloth showed ACT DR6 bounds on extra light particles hinge on inflation assumptions. ACT alone found no new light particles and a low expansion rate, confirming Hubble tension. Adding self-interacting dark radiation with running and running-of-running spectral indices relaxed the bound to under six-tenths and eased the tension to about two sigma with three extra parameters. If dark radiation couples to dark matter first and decouples near matter-radiation equality, the bound loosens further and tension falls below two sigma.
arxiv-2604-26741: Zheng, Zhu, Yuan, Hu, and Schmeink study uplink power control for integrated sensing, computing, and links in federated learning, where one waveform serves sensing, computing, and links through air computation. Edge devices transmit signals serving both sensing and merging, and the goal is minimizing merging error under a joint detection requirement. Though hard in original inputs, the problem admits a matching convex rewrite after input change. Exact best-case facts yield a robust, optimal, fast algorithm for transmit powers and receive scaling, checked in tests against rivals.
arxiv-2604-26841: Pham and four colleagues show that uniform-based discrete diffusion language models behave as associative memories, systems that recover stored items through basins of attraction. As training data grows, basins around training examples shrink while basins around unseen test examples expand, until both converge. The team detects this memorization-to-generalization shift using only the conditional entropy of predicted token sequences, which vanishes under memorization and stays finite under generalization. Conditional entropy thus offers a practical probe for deployed models.
arxiv-2604-27441: Aditya and five colleagues present ReVo, a resilient volumetric videoconferencing system that recovers RGB and depth under packet loss in real time on desktops. Volumetric video sends appearance and geometry for 6DoF, but packet loss degrades looks, corrupts geometry, and causes freezes. ReVo splits video into RGB and depth streams, protects critical content with error correction, and rebuilds corrupted frames with a recovery module over WebRTC. With real loss traces, it improves SSIM by up to 32 percent for RGB and 13 percent for depth, and cuts freezes by 95.7 percent against rivals.
arxiv-2604-27541: Robens reviews the hunt for light scalars at Higgs factories, the colliders built to study the Higgs boson in detail. She reviews the models that make such light scalars possible and the new work since an earlier review of the field. The note focuses on fresh developments rather than repeating the older survey in full. It gives readers a compact update on where the hunt for these particles now stands.
arxiv-2604-27741: Xu and Vreeken study where two populations differ in feature space, formalized as a differential subgroup. Such a subgroup holds people from both populations who share traits yet differ exceptionally in outcome. Differential subgroups reveal where gaps peak and which covariate combinations drive them, aiding clinics, diagnostics, and treatment work. They introduce an optimization objective for discovering subgroups and set conditions for a causal reading of gaps. DiffSub, their gradient-based tabular approach, finds subgroups across benchmarks, cases, errors, and treatment settings, showing where differences arise and why.
arxiv-2604-27841: Ben Rjeb and Tradacete map the free Banach lattice built from a distributive lattice, a structure that pairs lattice order with Banach size rules. They pin down when it holds a strong unit, work out its density character, and check order intervals plus how dense the free vector lattice sits inside it. They also chart projection bands, quasi-interior points, and maps born from lattice maps. Last, they show the lattice matches, by a lattice isometry, the free Banach lattice built from the flipped lattice.
arxiv-2604-28041: Barrios, Le Mouël and Carrillo sketch a computing continuum that weaves quantum processors into edge, cloud and high-performance systems. Three layers cover shared fibre hardware, user-run control and orchestration, and an adaptive setup fusing quantum and classical work. Tighter links, down to cryogenic logic, cut wasted energy and heat. The goal is an energy-per-problem edge for advanced computing.
arxiv-2604-28141: Yu and Zhao build an index-aided stratified sampling method for online aggregation, where approximate answers with confidence bounds must arrive fast over changing data. Classic stratified sampling with Neyman allocation minimises sample size in theory but needs prior statistics and costly optimisation. Their two-phase design uses first-phase samples both for answers and for optimising later strata. It proves optimal stratification and allocation for index-based costs and beats both uniform and scan-based baselines, dramatically in extreme cases.
arxiv-2605-00641:
Daniel Hangan, Stephen Kobourov, and Jacob Miller bridge two fields that solve the same problem in different dialects. Graph drawing and dimensionality reduction both lay out abstract structure in the plane. Multidimensional scaling, a classic embedding method, usually runs on the SMACOF algorithm. Graph drawing research, however, has long suggested simpler stochastic optimization can beat it on the very same stress objective.

The authors adapt stochastic gradient descent from graph drawing to vector data embedding, delivering an estimator compatible with the standard scikit-learn toolkit. Their solver minimizes global stress through local pairwise updates, refining an existing implementation. On standard high-dimensional benchmarks it converged substantially faster than SMACOF while reaching comparable or lower stress. The paper is a technology transfer with a moral: two literatures optimizing one objective should read each other, and a simpler borrowed algorithm can win.
arxiv-2605-00741:
Saeid Jamshidi and 3 co-authors let language-model agents choose security controls for Internet of Things systems, while a deterministic core keeps them safe. Edge IoT deployments need defenses that adapt at runtime, but choosing and combining mitigation actions under latency, energy, and computing limits, without unsafe interactions between controls, is a constrained decision problem. Static rule sets and learned policies offer few guarantees about feasibility or conflict safety.

Their system, ASPO, separates proposal from enforcement inside a standard self-adaptation loop. Language-model agents suggest portfolios of security patterns, and a deterministic optimizer then enforces action integrity, conflict-free composition, and resource feasibility at every decision step. Deployed on an edge-gateway testbed against replayed attack traffic, the system activated controls with perfect conflict freedom and consistent feasibility. Deeper exploration compressed the worst-case latency and energy overheads by about a fifth, at no increase in average energy use.
arxiv-2605-01341:
Anselm Haak, Patrick Koopmann, Yasir Mahmood, and Anni-Yasmin Turhan study abduction for knowledge bases. Given a database split into fixed rules and stored facts, the task is to find added facts that would make a target claim follow. The twist is that real data can clash, leaving the base inconsistent.

Most past work assumed clean, consistent bases. Here the authors define what abduction should mean when repairs are allowed. A repair trims the facts just enough to restore sense. They also set tests for what makes a guessed addition useful rather than trivial. They then map the computational cost of several forms of the problem for two light logics, DL-Lite and a variant of EL. The landscape tells system builders which forms of fault-finding and explanation stay feasible once bad data enters the base.
arxiv-2605-01541:
Giovanna Ilardi, Abbas Nasrollah Nejad, and Saeed Tafazolian introduce Veronese-avoiding hypersurfaces, a new class of surfaces guided by the theory of associated forms. The defining condition, rephrased through Macaulay inverse systems in the smooth case, amounts to the associated form being non-degenerate.

The main theorem handles the singular case. A reduced hypersurface with exactly as many isolated singular points as the dimension is of this kind exactly when those points are ordinary nodes in general linear position. Singular plane cubics are classified outright, and cases with fewer nodes are treated through a natural rational map. The space of such surfaces is shown to be locally closed, with a special nodal locus inside it. A Lefschetz-type result for the Milnor algebra in degree one closes the paper, tying the new class to classical singularity theory.
arxiv-2605-01941:
Arcangelo Massari and Silvio Peroni present HERITRACE, a web tool that lets people curate RDF data without deep Semantic Web training. RDF stores facts as linked triples, but editing it normally needs specialist skill. HERITRACE uses simple forms, records who changed what, and keeps a history that can be browsed or restored.

Forms and data rules come from SHACL shapes, and the tool connects to existing stores through SPARQL without moving the data. Setup is layered, from a basic link to a store up to custom display rules. The system already runs for the ParaText project on ancient Greek texts, with wider uses planned for citation and social science data.
arxiv-2605-02041:
Inoussa Mouiche and Sherif Saad present TIJERE, a model that pulls entities and their relations from cyber threat reports into structured form. Such extraction feeds knowledge graphs for threat analysis, but past joint methods suffer from confused features, ambiguous language, noise spread, and overlapping relations. TIJERE recasts the task with a multi-sequence labelling scheme, building a separate sequence for each entity pair.

Expert domain features enrich position, context, and meaning for each entity, which sharpens feature separation and classification. A security-tuned language model, SecureBERT+, helps reduce ambiguity and improve generalisation in the domain. The authors position TIJERE as a step toward more accurate automated threat intelligence processing.
arxiv-2605-02241:
Luong Nguyen asks how well a small language model can judge its own correctness, a skill that decides whether cheap local models can triage questions for costly cloud models. If a local model knows when it is likely wrong, hard queries can be escalated and easy ones kept local, with no supervised training data. Nguyen compares zero-shot confidence signals with supervised routing baselines in the style of RouteLLM.

Tests cover three model families at the seven to eight billion parameter scale and two data sets. Average token log-probability, which needs no training, matched or beat supervised baselines in distribution. Out of distribution it won by a wide margin. The author argues the signal works because it measures the generation itself, not the query.
arxiv-2605-02341:
Members of the ATLAS Collaboration extend a recent measurement from the Large Hadron Collider to probe how top quarks behave near the point where a top and antitop pair can just form. The study uses proton collisions and looks at pairs that decay to an electron and a muon. It asks whether a short-lived, loosely bound state forms near that threshold.

The team compares the measured shapes with model forecasts, with and without such a bound state included. The data fit the forecasts that include the state better, and a fit to the mass shape gives signs of the effect at more than three standard units of significance. The measured rate also matches dedicated studies of the same region.
arxiv-2605-02541:
Fayez Abu-Ajamieh assesses whether two X-ray missions could detect vacuum birefringence caused by magnetars, the strongly magnetic stars known as magnetars.
